source.title: On the Gross–Stark Conjecture
source.authors: Samit Dasgupta, Mahesh Kakde and Kevin Ventullo

summary:
Dasgupta, Kakde and Ventullo prove the Gross–Stark conjecture. Let F be a totally real field, χ a totally odd character of G_F cut out by the CM extension H/F, p a prime and E the finite extension of Q_p generated by the values of χ. Partition the primes of F above p into R = {p : χ(p) = 1} and R′, and write r = r_p(χ) = #R. Gross's regulator is R_p(χ) = det(ℓ_p^χ ∘ (o_p^χ)^{-1}) ∈ E, where o_p and ℓ_p are the valuation and the p-adic logarithm of the norm on the χ-component U_χ of the p-units of H; Gross's Conjecture 2 is L_p^{(r)}(χω, 0)/(r! L(χ, 0)) = R_p(χ) ∏_{p ∈ R′}(1 − χ(p)), for the Deligne–Ribet p-adic L-function. Theorem 1 proves it: L_an(χ) = R_p(χ). With the known inequality ord_{s=0} L_p(χω, s) ≥ r, Gross's Conjecture 1 becomes unconditionally equivalent to R_p(χ) ≠ 0. The rank one case was proved by Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack and Ventullo; the higher rank case had been thought unapproachable by their methods.

The proof. Any class κ ∈ H^1_R(G_F, V(χ^{-1})) unramified outside R is orthogonal to the p-units: Σ_{i=1}^r (res_{p_i} κ)(u) = 0 for u ∈ U_χ (Proposition 2.1, proved twice, once by Poitou–Tate duality and the Kummer map and once by class field theory alone). In rank one one constructs a cyclotomic class and reads L_an(χ) off its local restriction; for r > 1 the local restriction is no longer injective, and the authors do not know how to construct even one cyclotomic class. Instead they build a class κ with values in a module B̄ and use the orthogonality directly: the r resulting equations make a determinant vanish, and the determinant computes the regulator.

The class comes from Ribet's method. A linear combination of Eisenstein series and Ventullo's auxiliary family gives a cuspidal Hida family F of Hilbert modular forms specializing in weight one to the p-stabilized Eisenstein series E_1(1, χ_S). F is not an eigenform modulo π^{r+1}, so instead of an infinitesimal eigenform the authors study its whole Hecke orbit: the orbit is finite-dimensional over E[π]/π^{r_an+1} and yields Λ-algebra homomorphisms from the Hecke algebra onto explicit local Artin rings W_1, W_2, W_3 (Theorems 3.3, 3.6, 3.8, one for each of the three cases R′ ≠ ∅; R′ = ∅ with ν_1(W) ≠ 0; R′ = ∅ with ν_1(W) = 0), in which U_{p_i} ↦ 1 + ε_i and the single relation ε_1 ⋯ ε_r = −(−1)^{r_an} L*_an(χ) π^{r_an} carries the leading term of the p-adic L-function. The Galois representations of Wiles and Hida attached to the Hida eigenfamilies, glued over the reduced localized Hecke algebra, give the cocycle κ(σ) = b̄(σ)χ^{-1}(σ); Ribet's wrench and the ordinary local shape at p bound it (Lemmas 4.6–4.9), and applying the homomorphism to the vanishing determinant produces, in the one-dimensional space m_W^r/m_W^{r+1}, exactly the identity (−1)^{r+1} L_an(χ) det(o_i(u_j)) + det(ℓ_i(u_j)) = 0, which is Theorem 1. Case 3 needs the same argument run with the lower left entries of the representation in place of the upper right ones, which also fills a hole in the rank one paper (Remark 5.2).

What it needs. Almost nothing here is in the libraries. Mathlib has Dirichlet's unit theorem, the one library item; Tau Ceti has the local Teichmüller lift, the formal logarithm log(1+x) and Chebotarev infrastructure, but not the p-adic logarithm on Q_p^*, the Artin maps, Chebotarev's theorem, Hilbert modular forms, Hida theory or any p-adic L-function. The atlas plans the Deligne–Ribet L-function and the Hilbert Eisenstein series (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3), ordinary theory over totally real fields (PadicFamilies L5), Galois representations over ordinary Hecke algebras (OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.3), Poitou–Tate duality (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4) and Wiles's totally real main conjecture (IntegralIwasawaTheory I.5), but nothing plans the Gross–Stark conjecture itself. After the review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18) there are 125 items (2 library, 14 planned, 109 missing) and 35 source issues. E1 and E8 are rejected. The one substantive new finding is that the published Theorem 3.2 lost the normalisation ν_1(t)E_1(1, χ_S) = E_1(1, χ_S) of arXiv v1, which the later proofs need. Restoring it repairs them, and Theorem 1 stands. The other new findings are misprints and local slips that affect nothing.

items.name: The character χ and the field H
items.statement: F is a totally real number field, p an arbitrary prime number (p = 2 allowed), and χ : G_F → Q̄^* a continuous (hence finite-order) totally odd character of the absolute Galois group of F, i.e. χ(c_v) = −1 for the complex conjugation c_v attached to every real place v. H is the CM cyclic extension of F cut out by χ, the subfield of F̄ fixed by ker χ. G = Gal(H/F), so χ induces an injection G ↪ Q̄^*, and c ∈ G is the unique complex conjugation of H. Embeddings Q̄ ↪ C and Q̄ ↪ C_p are fixed once and for all, so χ may be read in C or in C_p.
items.note: Totally odd means odd at every archimedean place; H is CM because F is totally real and χ is totally odd, so complex conjugation is a single element c ∈ G independent of the place. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: Omits the prime p, which is part of the fixed data: p is an arbitrary prime, p = 2 included (the paper defines ω for p = 2 on p. 834 and takes u = 5 when p = 2 in §3.1). It also does not say that χ is continuous, hence of finite order, which is what makes H a finite cyclic extension.

items.name: The Artin L-function L(χ, s) and its Euler factors
items.statement: The complex Artin L-function L(χ, s) of the one-dimensional character χ, its analytic continuation and functional equation, and the convention adopted throughout the paper: χ(p) = 0 if p ramifies in H/F, and χ(p) = χ(Frob(p, H/F)) if p is unramified in H/F.
items.note: Read as the L-function of the associated ray-class character of F; the paper uses only its values at non-positive integers and the vanishing order at s = 0. Review note: Arguably planned rather than missing. AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1 plans 'the global integral Euler factorization, continuation and functional equation' of Tate zeta integrals of idele class characters, and tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalNumberFields#layer-9-hecke-and-ray-class-characters plans finite-order Hecke and ray-class characters with their conductors. Together with Artin reciprocity (tauceti ClassFieldTheory) they give L(χ, s), its continuation and its functional equation. Only the dictionary from Galois characters to ray-class characters and the paper's convention at ramified primes are left to AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L0.

items.name: The p-depleted L-function L*(χ, s)
items.statement: L*(χ, s) = L(χ, s) · ∏_{p | p} (1 − χ(p)(Np)^{−s}), the L-function of χ with the Euler factors at the primes above p removed.
items.note: Review note: 'Missing' is acceptable. AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3 plans the Deligne–Ribet interpolation 'including … Euler factors', which is exactly L*(χω^n, n), so L3 needs the same p-depleted L-function; L3 may be a better owner than L0.

items.name: L(χ, 0) ≠ 0 for totally odd χ
items.statement: For χ totally odd, L(χ, 0) ≠ 0. This follows from the functional equation for L(χ, s) together with the non-vanishing L(χ^{-1}, 1) ≠ 0.
items.note: Stated in the paper as well known, with no reference; L(χ, 0) appears in the denominator of both Conjecture 2 and L_an(χ), so the statement is needed for those to be defined. Review note: 'Missing' is right. The functional equation is planned (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1), but L(ψ, 1) ≠ 0 for a general nontrivial finite-order Hecke character is not. tauceti Chebotarev Layer 5 plans it only for the characters of cyclotomic extensions K(ζ_m)/K, and Mathlib's DirichletCharacter.LFunction_apply_one_ne_zero (LSeries/Nonvanishing.lean:408 at 082e2d3) covers only F = Q.

items.name: The Teichmüller character ω
items.statement: ω : G_F → μ_{p−1} (μ_2 if p = 2) is the Teichmüller character: the composite of the p-adic cyclotomic character ε_cyc : G_F → Z_p^* with the projection ω : Z_p^* → μ(Q_p) onto the torsion subgroup, i.e. ω(x) is the root of unity with ω(x) ≡ x mod p (mod 4 if p = 2). For x ∈ Z_p^*, ⟨x⟩ = x/ω(x) ∈ 1 + pZ_p (1 + 4Z_2 if p = 2), so x = ω(x)⟨x⟩. ω is totally odd (ω(c_v) = ω(−1) = −1), so ω^{-1} is itself a totally odd character.
items.note: Tau Ceti has the local Teichmüller lift `TauCeti.teichmuller : 𝓀[K]ˣ →* 𝒪[K]ˣ` (TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/Teichmuller.lean:100, read at f790474); the Galois character ω of G_F and the decomposition x = ω(x)⟨x⟩ are not in either library. DirichletPadicLFunctions L3 plans the Teichmüller decomposition of Z_p^*. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The gloss 'the composition of the cyclotomic character with the Teichmüller lift' is wrong for p = 2. The Teichmüller lift of F_2^* is trivial, but the paper's ω for p = 2 takes values in μ_2 = {±1}: it is the character of F(μ_4)/F. In every case ω is the cyclotomic character followed by the projection of Z_p^* onto its torsion subgroup. Review note: Planned is right in substance. DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 plans the Teichmüller decomposition of Z_p^*, and the Galois character is its composite with Mathlib's cyclotomicCharacter. But the cited TauCeti.teichmuller (NumberTheory/LocalField/Teichmuller.lean:100 at f790474) is the residue-field lift 𝓀[K]ˣ →* 𝒪[K]ˣ onto μ_{q−1}. For K = Q_2 that lift is trivial and does not give ω, so L3 must include the p = 2 decomposition Z_2^* = {±1} × (1 + 4Z_2).

items.name: Siegel's algebraicity theorem
items.statement: (Siegel; Klingen) For every finite-order character ψ of G_F and every n ∈ Z_{≤0}, L(ψ, n) is algebraic; indeed it lies in the field Q(ψ) generated by the values of ψ. Hence the values L*(χω^n, n) (n ∈ Z_{≤0}) and L(χ, 0) are algebraic, and through the fixed embedding Q̄ ↪ C_p they are read as p-adic numbers; in particular L(χ, 0) ∈ E.
items.note: Attributed to Siegel and used without reference. AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3 plans the algebraicity of negative critical values for a totally real field. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: As stated, the item gives only the algebraicity of L*(χω^n, n). That says nothing about L(χ, 0) when R ≠ ∅, because then L*(χ, 0) = 0. Yet (6), L_an(χ) and L*_an(χ) all divide by L(χ, 0) and treat it as an element of E ('the equality (6) takes place in the field E'). So the algebraicity of L(χ, 0) itself is needed, and Siegel's theorem also gives it. Review note: Planned is right: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3 plans 'the algebraicity of negative critical values' for a totally real field.

items.name: The Deligne–Ribet p-adic L-function
items.statement: For every totally odd χ there is a unique meromorphic p-adic L-function L_p(χω, s) on Z_p, determined by the interpolation property L_p(χω, n) = L*(χω^n, n) for all n ∈ Z_{≤0}. It is analytic on Z_p if χ ≠ ω^{-1}. For χ = ω^{-1} (χω = 1, the p-adic zeta function of F) it is analytic except for at most a simple pole at s = 1, and in particular it is analytic at s = 0. Its values and derivatives at the points where it is analytic lie in E = Q_p(χ). (Deligne–Ribet; Cassou-Noguès.)
items.note: Proved independently by Deligne–Ribet and Cassou-Noguès; the paper also cites the newer constructions of Charollois–Dasgupta, Spiess and Beilinson–Kings–Levin. Neither library has any p-adic L-function of a totally real field. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The item restricts to χ ≠ ω^{-1}, but the paper asserts a unique meromorphic L_p(χω, s) for every totally odd χ, analytic when χ ≠ ω^{-1}. Because ω^{-1} is totally odd, χ = ω^{-1} (χω = 1, the p-adic zeta function of F) is a legitimate case of Conjectures 1 and 2 and of Theorem 1 and must not be dropped. The item also leaves out that the values lie in E, which (6) uses. Review note: Planned is right. AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3 owns the Deligne–Ribet pseudo-measure; IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.3 imports it and includes the trivial-character pole.

items.name: The partition R ∪ R′ and the rank r_p(χ)
items.statement: The set of primes of F above p is partitioned as R ∪ R′, where R = {p | p : χ(p) = 1} and R′ = {p | p : χ(p) ≠ 1}; r_p(χ) = #R, written r throughout.
items.note: The primes in R are exactly those whose Euler factor in (2) vanishes at s = 0; the paper writes the empty set as φ, so 'R′ = φ' means R′ = ∅.

items.name: The order of vanishing of L*(χ, s) at s = 0
items.statement: ord_{s=0} L*(χ, s) = r_p(χ), since L(χ, 0) ≠ 0 and r_p(χ) is precisely the number of Euler factors above p in (2) that vanish at s = 0.

items.name: Gross's Conjecture 1 (the order of vanishing)
items.statement: ord_{s=0} L_p(χω, s) = r_p(χ).
items.note: Not proved in this paper. Theorem 1 makes it unconditionally equivalent to R_p(χ) ≠ 0.

items.name: The inequality ord_{s=0} L_p(χω, s) ≥ r_p(χ)
items.statement: ord_{s=0} L_p(χω, s) ≥ r_p(χ). For p ≠ 2 this follows from Wiles's proof of the Main Conjecture of Iwasawa theory for totally real fields; an analytic proof valid for all p was given by Charollois–Dasgupta and by Spiess, both resting on Spiess's results on cohomological p-adic L-functions.
items.note: Cited, not proved. IntegralIwasawaTheory I.5 plans Wiles's totally real main conjecture; the deduction of (4) from it (Ventullo §2.1) and the analytic proofs are not planned anywhere. Review note: The status should be 'missing', routed to IntegralIwasawaTheoryPartII with IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.5 as a prerequisite. I.5 plans Wiles's totally real main conjecture only at odd primes, and it does not plan the deduction of (4) (Ventullo §2.1). For p = 2 the paper relies on Charollois–Dasgupta [4, Th. 3] and Spiess [20], and no stage plans those; the all-prime main conjecture of IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.9 could replace them, but no stage plans that deduction either. (4) is on the path to the main results: §1.4 (p. 843) and §5.1 (p. 867) treat only r_an = r and r_an > r, and the equivalence of Conjecture 1 with R_p(χ) ≠ 0 (p. 837) uses (4) for every p. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): status changed from planned (IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.5) to missing. I.5 plans Wiles's totally real main conjecture at odd primes only and does not plan the deduction of (4) from it (Ventullo §2.1); for p = 2 the paper relies on Charollois–Dasgupta and Spiess, which no stage plans. Routed to IntegralIwasawaTheoryPartII, with I.5 (and I.9 for p = 2) as prerequisites.

items.name: Iwasawa's p-adic logarithm
items.statement: log_p : Q_p^* → Z_p, Iwasawa's p-adic logarithm, normalized so that log_p(p) = 0.
items.note: Tau Ceti has the formal logarithm `NormedSpace.logOneAdd` on a normed algebra (TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Algebra/LogOneAdd/Basic.lean:66, read at f790474), which gives log on the 1-units; the extension to Q_p^* with log_p(p) = 0 is not there. DirichletPadicLFunctions L3 plans exactly this normalization. Review note: Planned is right: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 says 'Fix log_p(p)=0 and the logarithm on all algebraic extensions compatibly'. The cited NormedSpace.logOneAdd (Analysis/Normed/Algebra/LogOneAdd/Basic.lean:66 at f790474) is only the series for log(1+u), and Mathlib at 082e2d3 has no p-adic logarithm.

items.name: The local maps o_P and ℓ_P
items.statement: For a prime P of O_H above p, the two continuous homomorphisms o_P = ord_P : H_P^* → Z and ℓ_P = log_p ∘ Norm_{H_P/Q_p} : H_P^* → Z_p.

items.name: The p-units U, the divisor group X and their minus parts
items.statement: U = O_H[1/p]^* is the group of p-units of H and X the free abelian group on the set S_p of primes of O_H above p, both G-modules. Their minus parts for the unique complex conjugation c ∈ G are U^- = {u ∈ U : c(u) = u^{-1}} and X^- = {x ∈ X : c(x) = −x}, and o_p : U^- → X^-, o_p(u) = (o_P(u))_P, ℓ_p : U^- → X^- ⊗ Z_p, ℓ_p(u) = (−ℓ_P(u))_P.
items.note: Note the sign in ℓ_p, which matches the sign in the numerator of (8).

items.name: o_p is a rational isomorphism of Q[G]-modules
items.statement: After tensoring with Q the map o_p induces a Q[G]-module isomorphism U^- ⊗ Q ≅ X^- ⊗ Q.
items.note: Cited to Tate's book on Stark's conjectures, I.4; a form of the Dirichlet S-unit theorem together with the finiteness of the class group.

items.name: The χ-components U_χ and X_χ
items.statement: E is the finite extension of Q_p generated by the values of χ, and U_χ = {u ∈ U^- ⊗ E : σ(u) = u^{χ^{-1}(σ)}}, X_χ = {x ∈ X^- ⊗ E : σ(x) = χ^{-1}(σ)x}. Both are E-vector spaces of dimension r_p(χ), and o_p, ℓ_p induce E[G]-module homomorphisms o_p^χ, ℓ_p^χ : U_χ → X_χ with o_p^χ an isomorphism.

items.name: Gross's p-adic regulator R_p(χ)
items.statement: R_p(χ) = det(ℓ_p^χ ∘ (o_p^χ)^{-1}) ∈ E, in parallel with the classical Stark regulator.
items.note: Footnote 1: this normalization differs from the regulator of Gross's paper by the factor (−1)^{r_p(χ)} ∏_{p | p} f_p, and is chosen to agree with Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack.

items.name: Gross's Conjecture 2 (the Gross–Stark conjecture)
items.statement: With r = r_p(χ), L_p^{(r)}(χω, 0) / (r! · L(χ, 0)) = R_p(χ) · ∏_{p ∈ R′} (1 − χ(p)), an equality in E. The statement does not depend on Conjecture 1.

items.name: The p-adic Gamma function
items.statement: Morita's p-adic Gamma function Γ_p : Z_p → Z_p^* is the unique continuous function with Γ_p(n) = (−1)^n ∏_{0<j<n, p∤j} j for every integer n ≥ 1. It satisfies Γ_p(0) = 1, Γ_p(x + 1) = −x Γ_p(x) for x ∈ Z_p^*, and Γ_p(x + 1) = −Γ_p(x) for x ∈ pZ_p.
items.note: Used only through the two cited theorems; not otherwise developed in the paper. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: Not an exact statement: it describes Γ_p instead of defining it. Review note: Context only: it enters only the historical proof for F = Q, which Theorem 1 subsumes. No stage plans Γ_p (DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 does not mention it), so 'missing' is right.

items.name: The Gross–Koblitz formula
items.statement: Let q = p^f. Fix π ∈ Q̄_p with π^{p−1} = −p and the p-th root of unity ζ_π ≡ 1 + π mod π^2, and let ω : F_q^* → μ_{q−1} be the Teichmüller character. For 0 ≤ a < q − 1, write the p-adic digits of a as a = a_0 + a_1p + ⋯ + a_{f−1}p^{f−1} and put s(a) = Σ a_i. Then Σ_{x ∈ F_q^*} ω(x)^{−a} ζ_π^{Tr_{F_q/F_p}(x)} = −π^{s(a)} ∏_{i=0}^{f−1} Γ_p(⟨p^i a/(q − 1)⟩), where ⟨y⟩ ∈ [0, 1) is the fractional part and Γ_p is Morita's p-adic Gamma function (Gross–Koblitz [12]).
items.note: Cited, not proved; an input to the case F = Q. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: Not an exact statement: it paraphrases the paper's one-line description. Review note: Context only (the F = Q case); not on the path to Theorem 1.

items.name: The Ferrero–Greenberg theorem
items.statement: Ferrero–Greenberg [9]: let F = Q and let χ be an odd Dirichlet character with χ(p) = 1, the exceptional case r_p(χ) = 1. Then L_p′(χω, 0) is expressed explicitly through the values log_p Γ_p(a/f), 0 < a < f, of the p-adic Gamma function, where f is the conductor of χ. Combined with the Gross–Koblitz formula and Brumer's theorem, this gives L_p′(χω, 0) ≠ 0, i.e. a simple zero of L_p(χω, s) at s = 0. The exact hypotheses on p are those of [9].
items.note: Cited, not proved; an input to the case F = Q. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The clause 'in particular L_p′(χω, 0) ≠ 0 for χ ≠ 1' is not in the paper and has the wrong hypothesis. A totally odd χ is never trivial, and the non-vanishing of L_p′(χω, 0) concerns the exceptional case χ(p) = 1 (r_p(χ) = 1). When χ(p) ≠ 1 the order of vanishing is 0, L_p(χω, 0) = L(χ, 0)(1 − χ(p)) ≠ 0, and nothing is asserted about L_p′. The item also omits that the theorem is about F = Q. Review note: Context only; not on the path to Theorem 1.

items.name: Gross's theorem: Conjectures 1 and 2 for F = Q
items.statement: Both conjectures hold when F = Q; Conjecture 2 follows by combining the Gross–Koblitz formula with the theorem of Ferrero–Greenberg. This special case motivated the general conjecture.
items.note: Review note: This paper subsumes it. Conjecture 2 for F = Q is the case F = Q of Theorem 1. Conjecture 1 for F = Q follows from (4), Theorem 1 and R_p(χ) ≠ 0 for r ≤ 1 (Gross, Prop. 2.13; over Q there is one prime above p, so r ≤ 1). No independent proof through Gross–Koblitz and Ferrero–Greenberg is needed; the item can be a corollary node of theorem-1.

items.name: Federer–Gross: equality of valuations
items.statement: When the order of χ divides p − 1, the p-adic valuations of the two sides of Conjecture 2 are equal; in particular, under that restriction Conjecture 1 is equivalent to R_p(χ) ≠ 0.
items.note: Cited to Federer–Gross, Proposition 3.10, proved there from the Iwasawa Main Conjecture. Review note: A corollary of Theorem 1: the two sides of (6) are equal, so a fortiori their valuations are. It needs no separate proof in the Part II.

items.name: The analytic L-invariant L_an(χ)
items.note: Written with a script L in the paper; distinct from the L-function L_p.

items.name: Theorem 1 — the Gross–Stark conjecture
items.statement: L_an(χ) = R_p(χ). Equivalently, Conjecture 2 holds for every totally odd character χ of the absolute Galois group of a totally real field and every prime p.
items.note: The main theorem of the paper. The rank one case was proved by Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack under hypotheses later removed by Ventullo.

items.name: Conjecture 1 is equivalent to R_p(χ) ≠ 0
items.statement: In view of (4) and Theorem 1, Conjecture 1 holds if and only if R_p(χ) ≠ 0; this is known for r ≤ 1.
items.note: The case r ≤ 1 is Gross, Proposition 2.13, and yields Conjecture 1 for F = Q. Review note: The cited fact 'known for r ≤ 1' (R_p(χ) ≠ 0 when r ≤ 1, Gross [11, Prop. 2.13], which uses Brumer's theorem for r = 1) is a separate result and should be its own item; see coverage.

items.name: Remark 1.1 — the characteristic polynomial of the regulator matrix
items.statement: The endomorphism ℓ_p^χ ∘ (o_p^χ)^{-1} of X_χ is canonically defined, and so is its conjugate (o_p^χ)^{-1} ∘ ℓ_p^χ of U_χ, which has the same characteristic polynomial. Its determinant is R_p(χ), so one may ask for its characteristic polynomial and not only its determinant. Dasgupta–Spiess [6] conjecture a formula for that characteristic polynomial in terms of the Eisenstein cocycle, generalizing the Gross–Stark conjecture; the paper records that conjecture as open.
items.note: Recorded as context: an open conjecture, not a result of this paper. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: Reproduces the paper's misprint (new issue below): ℓ_p^χ ∘ (o_p^χ)^{-1} maps X_χ → U_χ → X_χ, so it is an endomorphism of X_χ, not of U_χ.

items.name: The maps o_i and ℓ_i attached to the primes of R
items.statement: For R = {p_1, …, p_r} and each p_i, o_i = ord_{p_i} : F_{p_i}^* → Z and ℓ_i = log_p ∘ Norm_{F_{p_i}/Q_p} : F_{p_i}^* → Z_p. After choosing a prime P_i of H above p_i the embedding O_H[1/p] ⊂ H ⊂ H_{P_i} ≅ F_{p_i} — an isomorphism because χ(p_i) = 1, so p_i splits completely in H/F — lets o_i and ℓ_i be evaluated on p-units and extended E-linearly to o_i, ℓ_i : O_H[1/p]^* ⊗ E → E.
items.note: The identification H_{P_i} ≅ F_{p_i} is used silently; it holds because p_i ∈ R. Review note: Status missing is right. These are the maps o_P, ℓ_P of item local-maps at P = P_i, read through H_{P_i} = F_{p_i}, which holds because χ(p_i) = 1 (p_i splits completely in H/F); this also holds for p = 2, where log_2(Q_2^*) ⊂ 4Z_2 ⊂ Z_2. log_p is planned at DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 (item iwasawa-log).

items.name: The regulator as a ratio of determinants
items.statement: For any E-basis u_1, …, u_r of U_χ, R_p(χ) = det(−ℓ_i(u_j))_{i,j} / det(o_i(u_j))_{i,j} ∈ E. The ratio is independent of the basis, and independent of the choice of P_i because replacing P_i by σ(P_i) scales the ith row of both matrices by χ(σ).
items.note: Review note: Statement and sign checked. The paper gives no proof, and this computation supplies one. For each i, x_i = Σ_{σ∈G} χ(σ)[σ(P_i)] lies in X_χ, and these r elements form a basis. The χ^{-1}-part of the divisors above R′ is zero because χ is nontrivial on their decomposition groups. For u ∈ U_χ, ord_{σ(P_i)}(u) = ord_{P_i}(σ^{-1}u) = χ(σ)o_i(u), and similarly for ℓ, so o_p^χ(u) = Σ_i o_i(u)x_i and ℓ_p^χ(u) = Σ_i (−ℓ_i(u))x_i. Hence (8) is det(ℓ_p^χ∘(o_p^χ)^{-1}) computed in the bases {u_j}, {x_i}. The claim about rescaling by χ(σ) is also correct. Status missing.

items.name: Non-vanishing of det(o_i(u_j))
items.statement: det(o_i(u_j)) ≠ 0: the χ^{-1}-component of the group of p_i-units of H is one-dimensional for each p_i ∈ R, so for a suitable basis {u_i} the matrix (o_i(u_j)) is the identity.
items.note: Deduced in the paper from the Dirichlet unit theorem; the statement actually needed is the S-unit theorem together with the semisimple decomposition of the E[G]-module U ⊗ E. Review note: True. A shorter proof than the paper's: by the computation under regulator-determinant, det(o_i(u_j)) is the determinant of o_p^χ in the bases {u_j}, {x_i}, and it is nonzero because o_p^χ is an isomorphism (items op-iso and chi-components, (5)). The paper's route through p_i-units needs three inputs: the finiteness of the class group, to get a p_i-unit of valuation h at P_i; Dirichlet's theorem in its CM form, that c acts trivially on O_H^*⊗Q, so that (O_H^*⊗E)^{χ^{-1}} = 0 (see the new coverage item); and the fact that the resulting u_i satisfy o_j(u_i) = 0 for j ≠ i and o_i(u_i) ≠ 0. Status missing.

items.name: Dirichlet's unit theorem
items.statement: For a number field K the unit group of O_K modulo torsion is free of rank r_1 + r_2 − 1 = #{infinite places} − 1.
items.note: Mathlib at 082e2d3: `NumberField.Units.rank` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Units/DirichletTheorem.lean:359), with `NumberField.Units.unitLattice_rank` (:385) and `NumberField.Units.finrank_modTorsion` (:458) — the earlier name `rank_modTorsion` is deprecated there. The S-unit theorem the paper needs is a separate item. Review note: Library status confirmed. I opened the declarations at 082e2d3 in Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Units/DirichletTheorem.lean. NumberField.Units.rank (:359) is the definition `Fintype.card (InfinitePlace K) - 1`. unitLattice_rank (:385) is finrank ℤ (unitLattice K) = rank K. finrank_modTorsion (:457) is finrank ℤ (Additive ((𝓞 K)ˣ ⧸ torsion K)) = rank K, and rank_modTorsion is its deprecated alias (:460). Freeness is the anonymous instance Module.Free ℤ (Additive ((𝓞 K)ˣ ⧸ torsion K)) at :431, with the named basis basisModTorsion at :466. Together these state what the item says. The paper actually uses (p. 838) the CM consequence: c acts trivially on O_H^*⊗Q, so the odd χ^{-1}-component vanishes. Mathlib has the inputs for that in Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/CMField.lean: NumberField.IsCMField.units_rank_eq_units_rank (:115) and indexRealUnits_eq_one_or_two (:374). See the new coverage item.

items.name: The S-unit theorem with its Galois module structure
items.statement: For S the set of archimedean places of H together with S_p, the group of S-units of H modulo torsion is free of rank #S − 1, and U^- ⊗ Q ≅ X^- ⊗ Q as Q[G]-modules, so that dim_E U_χ = dim_E X_χ = r_p(χ) and the χ^{-1}-component of the p_i-units is one-dimensional.
items.note: Neither library has the S-unit theorem; Mathlib has the case S = ∞ (see the item dirichlet-unit-theorem). Review note: Status missing is right. At f790474 Tau Ceti has the finite generation of S-units, Set.unit_fg_of_units (TauCeti/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/SInteger/Unit.lean:207) and Set.unit_fg (:149), and the kernel of the valuation map, Set.unitValuation_ker (:130). Its docstring says it is not the S-unit theorem: no rank is computed. Mathlib has only the definition Set.unit (Mathlib/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/SInteger.lean:108). The second half of the statement (U^-⊗Q ≅ X^-⊗Q, induced by o_p) is item op-iso ((5), pp. 835–836). This item should cite op-iso rather than restate it.

items.name: Compatible decomposition and inertia groups
items.statement: For each place v of F a decomposition group G_v ⊂ G_F is chosen, with inertia subgroup I_v ⊂ G_v; this is an embedding F̄ ⊂ F̄_v and specifies a prime of H above v. For p_i ∈ R the specified prime is the P_i of (7).
items.note: Review note: Looks planned by ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2, which plans 'Use a place or an embedding into a local separable closure to obtain restriction; prove invariance under changing that choice'.

items.name: The twisted Galois modules V(χ^{-1}) and V(χ)(1)
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional E-vector space V with its p-adic topology, V(χ^{-1}) is V with the continuous E-linear G_F-action σ·v = χ^{-1}(σ)v. E(χ)(1) is E with G_F acting by χ(σ)ε_cyc(σ), and V(χ)(1) is defined in the same way. All cohomology is continuous cochain cohomology.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The paper does not specify a topology on V, but the continuous cohomology H^1(G_F, V(χ^{-1})) depends on it. For example, with the discrete topology every continuous homomorphism to V has finite image, so it is zero. Every use in the paper has V finite-dimensional over E: V = E, and V = B̄ = B/m̂B, which is finite-dimensional because B is finitely generated over T_m (item cocycle-kappa). So the statement should fix V as a finite-dimensional E-vector space with its p-adic topology. Review note: Status missing.

items.name: Cohomology unramified outside R
items.statement: H^1_R(G_F, V(χ^{-1})) ⊂ H^1(G_F, V(χ^{-1})) is the subspace of continuous cohomology classes κ that are unramified outside R, i.e. res_{I_v} κ ∈ H^1(I_v, V(χ^{-1})) is trivial for all v ∉ R.
items.note: Review note: Correct. At the archimedean places the condition is automatic, including for p = 2, because H^1 of a group of order ≤ 2 with coefficients in an E-vector space vanishes. The general notion (Selmer-type subspaces cut out by local conditions, and cohomology with restricted ramification) looks planned by ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.3 and R02.5. This particular subspace is correctly marked missing.

items.name: The local cohomology at a prime of R
items.statement: For p_i ∈ R one has χ(G_{p_i}) = 1, so H^1(G_{p_i}, E(χ^{-1})) = H^1(G_{p_i}, E) = Hom_cts(G_{p_i}, E) ≅ Hom_cts(F̂_{p_i}^*, E), the last isomorphism by local class field theory.
items.note: Review note: Correct. The final isomorphism Hom_cts(G_{p_i}, E) ≅ Hom_cts(F̂^*_{p_i}, E) needs rec to identify the profinite completion F̂^* with G^{ab}. Tau Ceti's ClassFieldTheory plans that comparison at Layer 8 ('for K/ℚ_p finite, injectivity of the absolute artinMap and the comparison with the profinite completion of Kˣ, both of which follow from localAbelianExistence'), not at Layer 7. Status missing, since the item is a direct consequence of Layer 8.

items.name: The local reciprocity map, in Serre's normalization
items.statement: The local Artin map rec_{p_i} : F̂_{p_i}^* → G_{p_i}^{ab} on the profinite completion F̂_{p_i}^* = lim_m F_{p_i}^*/(F_{p_i}^*)^m, normalized as in Serre's Corps locaux: for u ∈ O_{F_p}^*, ε_cyc(rec(u)) = Norm_{O_{F_p}/Z_p} u, and rec(ϖ^{-1}) lifts the Frobenius of the maximal unramified extension for a uniformizer ϖ.
items.note: The normalization is stated in a footnote and matters for every sign in §5. Tau Ceti's ClassFieldTheory plans the absolute local Artin map and its normalizations at Layer 7; neither library has it at f790474. Review note: The statement is faithful to footnote 3, and the two stated formulas are consistent with each other: both are the 'geometric' normalisation. Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 7 plans the arithmetic artinMap, with χ_cyc(Art_K(u)) = N_{K/ℚ_p}(u)^{-1}, and defines geometricArtinMap as its precomposition with inversion. The paper's rec is therefore Layer 7's geometricArtinMap. The extension to the profinite completion F̂^* ≅ G^{ab}, which the item and local-h1 use, is Layer 8 (#layer-8-separate-arithmetic-local-existence-and-the-local-class-field-correspondence), so that layer should be added to 'planned'.

items.name: o_i and ℓ_i as characters of the profinite completion
items.statement: o_i and ℓ_i are continuous for the topology on F_{p_i}^* defined by the subgroups (F_{p_i}^*)^m, so they induce continuous homomorphisms o_i : F̂_{p_i}^* → Ẑ → Z_p and ℓ_i : F̂_{p_i}^* → Z_p.
items.note: Review note: Checked for every p, including p = 2. o_i^{-1}(mZ) ⊇ (F^*)^m. ℓ_i^{-1}(p^kZ_p) is the kernel of a map to Z_p/p^k, so it contains (F^*)^{p^k}. Status missing.

items.name: The cyclotomic subspace H^1_cyc(χ)
items.statement: H^1_cyc(χ) ⊂ H^1_R(G_F, E(χ^{-1})) is the set of κ such that for each p_i ∈ R the restriction res_{p_i} κ ∈ H^1(G_{p_i}, E) lies in the E-span of o_i and ℓ_i, viewed as continuous homomorphisms F̂_{p_i}^* → E.

items.name: dim_E H^1_cyc(χ) = r
items.statement: The space of cyclotomic classes has dimension r over E.
items.note: The paper calls this a straightforward generalization of Lemma 1.5 of Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack and gives no proof; it is used for the definition of L_alg(χ) and for det(y_ij) ≠ 0. Review note: True for every p, including p = 2; the paper only cites [5, Lemma 1.5]. Proof. By class field theory for the extension K of (24), restriction to the inertia groups identifies H^1_R(G_F, E(χ^{-1})) with ⊕_{i=1}^r Hom_cts(O^*_{F_{p_i}}, E). Surjectivity uses the fact that the image of the global units drops out on χ^{-1}-parts: H is CM and χ is odd, so Σ_τ χ(τ)τ(ε) = 0 in O_H^*⊗E for every unit ε. It also uses the finiteness of Cl_H and unique divisibility to extend from ∏_{w∈R_H} O_w^* to Gal(K/H), and the inflation–restriction isomorphism. A class lies in H^1_cyc exactly when each inertial component is a multiple y_iℓ_i|_{O^*}, which is automatic because F̂^* = O^*×ϖ^Ẑ and o_i(ϖ) = 1. So H^1_cyc ≅ E^r via κ ↦ (y_1, …, y_r). Injectivity of this map is also Proposition 2.2. The general computation gives dim_E H^1_R(G_F, E(χ^{-1})) = Σ_i [F_{p_i}:Q_p]. Status missing. The result is not on the path to Theorem 1.

items.name: The algebraic L-invariant L_alg(χ)
items.statement: For a basis κ_1, …, κ_r of H^1_cyc(χ) write res_{p_j} κ_i = x_ij o_j + y_ij ℓ_j with x_ij, y_ij ∈ E. Then L_alg(χ) = det(x_ij)/det(y_ij), after Greenberg's study of exceptional zeroes.
items.note: Review note: The definition is independent of the basis: changing {κ_i} multiplies both (x_ij) and (y_ij) on the left by the same invertible matrix. Status missing.

items.name: Non-vanishing of det(y_ij)
items.statement: det(y_ij)_{i,j=1…r} ≠ 0, using the linear independence of κ_1, …, κ_r together with dim_E H^1_cyc(χ) = r.
items.note: Asserted without proof. Review note: True. Proof (forward reference to Proposition 2.2, with no circularity): on the inertia subgroup (the units, through rec) o_j vanishes and ℓ_j does not, so res_{I_{p_j}}κ_i = y_ij·ℓ_j|_{O^*}. If Σ_i c_i(y_i1, …, y_ir) = 0, then Σ c_iκ_i is trivial on every I_{p_j}, hence zero by Proposition 2.2, hence c = 0. This does not even need dim H^1_cyc = r. Status missing.

items.name: Proposition 1 = Proposition 2.1 (orthogonality)
items.statement: Let κ ∈ H^1_R(G_F, V(χ^{-1})) and u ∈ U_χ. Viewing u as an element of F̂_{p_i}^* ⊗ E via (7), Σ_{i=1}^r (res_{p_i} κ)(u) = 0.
items.note: The engine of the whole proof; two proofs are given in §2. Review note: Both proofs checked, for all p. Proof 2 is complete given two inputs: global class field theory with the closure in (24) (see global-reciprocity), and the local–global compatibility of the reciprocity maps, which is needed for (res_Hκ)(rec(π_u)) = Σ_{w∈R_H}(res_wκ)(u). The conclusion is a vanishing statement, so it is insensitive to the arithmetic or geometric normalisation of rec and to the sign in (22). Status missing.

items.name: L_alg(χ) = R_p(χ)
items.statement: The orthogonality of Proposition 1 implies L_alg(χ) = R_p(χ).
items.note: Asserted as an easy consequence ('one readily proves'), with no computation given. It is not used in the proof of Theorem 1, which computes with the class κ directly. Review note: Checked, including the sign. Write X = (x_ij), Y = (y_ij), O = (o_j(u_k))_{j,k} and Λ = (ℓ_j(u_k))_{j,k}. Proposition 1 applied to κ_i and u_k gives XO + YΛ = 0, so X = −YΛO^{-1}. Hence det X/det Y = det(−Λ)/det(O) = R_p(χ) by (8), using det Y ≠ 0 and det O ≠ 0. Status missing. The note is right that Theorem 1 does not use this item.

items.name: The rank one strategy and its obstruction
items.statement: When r = 1 and R = {p}, Conjecture 2 is equivalent to the existence of a nonzero class κ ∈ H^1_cyc(χ) with res_p κ = L_an(χ) o_p + ℓ_p, which is what Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack and Ventullo construct. That construction relies on the injectivity of the local restriction H^1_R(G_F, E(χ^{-1})) → H^1(G_p, E) for R = {p}, which fails in general for a fixed p ∈ R when r > 1; the authors do not know how to construct even one cyclotomic class in the general case, and believe the analogous inclusion x_i B ⊂ m to be false for r ≥ 3.
items.note: Recorded because it fixes what the new method must avoid. Footnote 4 adds that if r = 2 and F_{p_i} ≅ Q_p for i = 1, 2 then (11) is injective and a proof in the style of [5] is possible. Review note: Correct as a record. Footnote 4 (r = 2, F_{p_i} ≅ Q_p ⇒ (11) injective) is true but not proved in the paper, and it needs a transcendence input. By the computation under h1-cyc-dimension, dim H^1_R = 2 = dim H^1(G_{p_1}, E). The kernel of res_{p_1} consists of the classes (0, c·log) with c·ℓ_2(u_1) = 0, where u_1 ∈ U_χ is the p_1-unit with o_1(u_1) = 1 (use Proposition 1 with u_1). So injectivity ⟺ ℓ_2(u_1) = Σ_τ χ(τ)log_p(τ(v))/h ≠ 0, which follows from Brumer's p-adic Baker theorem. Baker–Brumer is planned at IntegralIwasawaTheory:L4. None of this is used on the path to Theorem 1. Status missing.

items.name: The Kummer isomorphisms δ and δ_v
items.statement: Hilbert's Theorem 90 yields isomorphisms δ : (H^* ⊗̂ E)_{χ^{-1}} ≅ H^1(G_F, E(χ)(1)) and, locally, δ_v : (H_w^* ⊗̂ E)_{χ^{-1}} ≅ H^1(G_v, E(χ)(1)), where H^* ⊗̂ E = (lim_n (H^* ⊗ O_E/p^n)) ⊗_{O_E} E.
items.note: Cited to Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack, Proposition 1.4. The paper says explicitly that in Proof 1 'we state without proof certain identifications that are needed'. Review note: Faithful. The paper writes the eigenspace with a superscript χ^{-1}, meaning σx = χ^{-1}(σ)x; the item's subscript notation denotes the same space. Status missing is right. The finite-level Kummer isomorphism H^1(G_K, μ_n) ≅ K^*/K^{*n} is planned at tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-9-the-galois-interface-hilbert-90-and-kummer-theory. The inverse-limit comparison is planned at ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1. The χ-twisted rational version (18)–(19) is planned nowhere. It is used only in Proof 1, which Proof 2 makes unnecessary.

items.name: δ identifies U_χ with H^1_R(G_F, E(χ)(1))
items.statement: Defining H^1_R(G_F, E(χ)(1)) as the classes whose restriction at each v ∉ R lies in the image of (O_{H,w}^* ⊗̂ E)_{χ^{-1}} under δ_v, the map δ induces an isomorphism δ : U_χ ≅ H^1_R(G_F, E(χ)(1)).
items.note: Review note: True. 'It is then clear' hides four ingredients: the finiteness of Cl_H; O_{H,w}^*⊗̂E = 0 for w ∤ p, so the condition at such v forces the local class to vanish; the vanishing of the χ^{-1}-part of the divisors above R′; and (O_H^*⊗E)^{χ^{-1}} = 0. Status missing. It is used only in Proof 1.

items.name: Local Tate duality at the primes of R
items.statement: For each p_i ∈ R there is a perfect pairing ⟨ , ⟩_{p_i} : H^1(G_{p_i}, E(χ)(1)) × H^1(G_{p_i}, E(χ^{-1})) → E.
items.note: ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4 plans local duality and its rational-coefficient versions; neither library has continuous Galois cohomology duality at the pinned commits. Review note: The status is right but the planned stage is wrong. ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.4 plans Poitou–Tate duality 'from the global class-field-theory and local-duality inputs', so local duality is an input there, not something it plans. Finite-module local duality is tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-5-local-coefficients-the-brauer-group-the-local-invariant-and-duality (tateDualityPairing_perfect_mixed). The passage to lattice and rational coefficients is ArithmeticGaloisDuality:D7 ('derived local and global duality … finite, compact and discrete torsion formulations'). Cite those two stages. Since χ(G_{p_i}) = 1, the pairing is H^1(G_{p_i}, E(1)) × H^1(G_{p_i}, E) → E. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): planned stages changed from ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.4 to the ClassFieldTheory Layer 5 duality (finite modules) and ArithmeticGaloisDuality:D7 (lattice and rational coefficients). R02.4 takes local duality as an input to Poitou–Tate duality rather than planning it.

items.name: Poitou–Tate orthogonality of the restricted subspaces
items.statement: The images of H^1_R(G_F, V(χ^{-1})) and H^1_R(G_F, E(χ)(1)) under the product of the restriction maps res_{p_i} are orthogonal under the sum of the local Tate pairings ⟨ , ⟩_R : ∏_i H^1(G_{p_i}, V(χ^{-1})) × ∏_i H^1(G_{p_i}, E(χ)(1)) → V.
items.note: Deduced from Poitou–Tate duality, which R02.4 plans together with the nine-term exact sequence. The paper states it without proof. Review note: True; planned status acceptable (R02.4 plans the lattice and rational versions of Poitou–Tate). The paper says only 'it follows from Poitou–Tate duality'. The deduction has two parts. The first is the global reciprocity law Σ_v inv_v(a_v ∪ b_v) = 0 for global classes (ClassFieldTheory Layer 10, the Brauer sequence). The second is the vanishing of every local term at v ∉ R. At v ∈ R′, res_vκ ∈ H^1_ur(G_v, V(χ^{-1})) = 0, because χ is ramified at v or χ(Frob_v) ≠ 1. At finite v ∤ p outside R, res_vδ(u) lies in δ_v(O_w^*⊗̂E) = 0. At archimedean v, H^1 with E-coefficients vanishes, also for p = 2. These local steps should be written into the node's proof. For the order of the arguments, see the new issue on ⟨ , ⟩_{p_i}.

items.name: Compatibility of the Tate pairing with evaluation
items.statement: For κ ∈ H^1_R(G_F, V(χ^{-1})), u ∈ U_χ and p_i ∈ R, let res_{p_i}δ(u) = δ_{p_i}(u) with u viewed in (H_{P_i}^*⊗̂E) = (F_{p_i}^*⊗̂E) through (7). Take the pairing with the V(χ^{-1})-class in the first slot, that is cup product followed by inv_{p_i}. Then ⟨res_{p_i}κ, res_{p_i}δ(u)⟩_{p_i} = ε·(res_{p_i}κ)(u), where ε ∈ {±1} depends only on the conventions for δ, ∪, inv and rec, and not on i, κ or u. In particular Σ_i ⟨res_{p_i}κ, res_{p_i}δ(u)⟩_{p_i} = 0 ⟺ Σ_i (res_{p_i}κ)(u) = 0.
items.note: One of the identifications stated without proof in Proof 1; it is what makes the abstract duality statement compute the numbers of Proposition 1. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The item takes κ ∈ H^1(G_{p_i}, V(χ^{-1})), which is already a local class, and then applies res_{p_i} to it. The item also omits that (22) holds only up to a universal sign. That sign is fixed by the normalisations of δ, the cup product, inv and rec, which the paper never pins down. Moreover (22) puts κ in the first slot, whereas ⟨ , ⟩_{p_i} is displayed with the E(χ)(1)-class first, and swapping the two H^1 arguments changes the sign. Only the sign-independent consequence is used. Review note: Status missing is right. I found no atlas stage that names the identity inv(δ(a) ∪ f) = ±f(rec(a)). Its two ingredients are planned: ClassFieldTheory Layer 5 plans localSymbol (Kummer cup product followed by inv), and Layer 7 plans artinMap.

items.name: The restriction of κ to G_H and its equivariance
items.statement: For κ ∈ H^1_R(G_F, V(χ^{-1})), res_H κ ∈ H^1(G_H, V(χ^{-1}))^G = Hom_cts(G_H, V)^{χ^{-1}}, the space of continuous homomorphisms f : G_H → V with f(σhσ^{-1}) = χ^{-1}(σ) f(h) for σ ∈ G_F, h ∈ G_H; and res_H κ is trivial on I_w for every place w of H not above a place of R.
items.note: Review note: Checked: for h ∈ G_H, κ(σhσ^{-1}) = κ(σ) + χ^{-1}(σ)(κ(h) + κ(σ^{-1})) = χ^{-1}(σ)κ(h), since 0 = κ(σσ^{-1}) = κ(σ) + χ^{-1}(σ)κ(σ^{-1}). This is (23), and it agrees with the G-invariants of H^1(G_H, V(χ^{-1})). Status missing.

items.name: Global class field theory for the ray class field K
items.statement: Let R_H be the set of places of H above R, and K the maximal abelian extension of H unramified outside R_H. H is totally complex, so there is no archimedean condition. The global reciprocity map induces an isomorphism of topological groups rec : A_H^*/closure(H^*·∏_{w∉R_H}O_{H,w}^*) ≅ Gal(K/H), with O_{H,w}^* = C^* at complex places. For every finite place w, the restriction of rec to H_w^*, embedded with component 1 elsewhere, equals the local reciprocity map rec_w : H_w^* → G_w^{ab}, taken in the same normalisation as footnote 3, followed by the map to Gal(K/H) induced by the chosen decomposition group G_w ⊂ G_H.
items.note: Tau Ceti's ClassFieldTheory plans global Artin reciprocity at Layer 11 and class fields at Layer 13; neither library has them at f790474. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: Two omissions. First, the page image shows an overline over H^*∏_{w∉R_H}O_{H,w}^* in (24): the quotient is by the closure. The item drops the closure, and without it the statement is false once [H:Q] ≥ 4. There the image of the infinite, finitely generated unit group O_H^* in the profinite group ∏_{w∈R_H}O_{H,w}^* is infinite and countable, hence not closed (Baire). So H^*∏_{w∉R_H}O_{H,w}^* is not closed, and the natural surjection onto Gal(K/H) is not injective. Second, Proof 2 also needs the compatibility of rec with the local reciprocity maps. The name 'ray class field' is also inaccurate: K is the infinite union of the ray class fields of moduli supported on R_H. Review note: Planned status acceptable with a caveat. Layer 11 plans global reciprocity only for finite L/K (C_K/N_{L/K}C_L ≃ Gal(L/K)^{ab}), together with the local compatibility globalArtinMap_local. Layer 13 plans ray class fields of a single modulus. The passage to the limit over moduli supported on R_H, which produces the closure, is named in neither. Note also that Layer 11 normalises by arithmetic Frobenius (globalArtinMap_isArithFrobAt), while the paper uses the geometric map locally. Proof 2 is insensitive to this choice, but the local and global maps must use the same convention.

items.name: Proof 2 of Proposition 2.1 by class field theory
items.statement: For u an R_H-unit of H, the idèle π_u with component u at each w ∈ R_H and 1 elsewhere is trivial in the quotient (24), so 0 = (res_H κ)(rec(π_u)) = Σ_{w ∈ R_H} (res_w κ)(u) = Σ_{i=1}^r Σ_{σ ∈ G} (res_{σ(P_i)} κ)(u). Using res_{σ(P_i)}(u) = χ^{-1}(σ) res_{P_i}(σ^{-1}(u)) and res_{P_i} = res_{p_i} gives Σ_i (res_{p_i} κ)(u_χ) = 0 for u_χ = Σ_σ σ(u) ⊗ χ(σ), and such u_χ generate U_χ.
items.note: This second proof uses only class field theory and is self-contained; the first needs the unproved identifications above. Review note: Checked. Every prime above p_i is σ(P_i) for exactly one σ ∈ G, since p_i splits completely. The idele π_u equals u·(u^{-1} at every w ∉ R_H), which lies in H^*∏_{w∉R_H}O_{H,w}^*. By (23) and rec_{σP}(σx) = σ rec_P(x)σ^{-1}, (res_{σ(P_i)}κ)(u) = χ^{-1}(σ)(res_{P_i}κ)(σ^{-1}u), so Σ_σ(res_{σ(P_i)}κ)(u) = (res_{P_i}κ)(Σ_τ τ(u)⊗χ(τ)). The spanning claim (the u_χ generate U_χ) is proposed as a new coverage item. The step (res_Hκ)(rec(π_u)) = Σ_w(res_wκ)(u) uses the local–global compatibility now written into global-reciprocity. Status missing.

items.name: Proposition 2.2 (injectivity of the product of inertia restrictions)
items.statement: For an E-vector space V the restriction map ∏_{i=1}^r res_{I_{p_i}} : H^1_R(G_F, V(χ^{-1})) → ∏_{i=1}^r H^1(I_{p_i}, V) is injective.
items.note: Equivalently: there is no nonzero everywhere-unramified class. This is the substitute for the rank one injectivity (11) that fails for r > 1; it is used in Lemma 4.8. Review note: Proof checked. An unramified-everywhere class has res_Hκ trivial on every I_w: for w above R this follows from res_{I_{p_i}}κ = 0 together with (23). H is totally complex, so no archimedean ramification arises, and res_Hκ factors through the finite group Gal(Hilbert class field/H). Status missing.

items.name: res_H is an isomorphism on χ^{-1}-parts
items.statement: res_H : H^1(G_F, V(χ^{-1})) → H^1(G_H, V)^{χ^{-1}} is an isomorphism, because the neighbouring terms in the inflation–restriction sequence are H^i(G, V(χ^{-1})) for i = 1, 2, which vanish as G is finite and V is a torsion-free E-vector space.
items.note: Review note: The locator is wrong: the whole proof of Proposition 2.2 is on p. 845 (PDF page 13), and p. 846 begins §3. The vanishing of H^i(G, V(χ^{-1})) needs V to be uniquely divisible (a Q-vector space), which it is. Mere torsion-freeness, as the paper puts it, would not suffice: H^2(G, Z) ≠ 0. For coefficients that are not discrete, this looks planned by ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.2 (low-degree Hochschild–Serre and descent for finite extensions of number fields) and D7 (continuous five-term sequence). tauceti ProfiniteCohomology Layer 5 plans the five-term sequence only for discrete coefficients, and V is not discrete.

items.name: Finiteness of the Hilbert class field
items.statement: The maximal abelian unramified extension of H is a finite extension of H, so a continuous homomorphism from its Galois group to a torsion-free E-vector space vanishes.
items.note: Tau Ceti's ClassFieldTheory plans the Hilbert class field at Layer 13. Review note: The locator is wrong for the same reason as inflation-restriction: the text is on p. 845. The planned stage is right: ClassFieldTheory Layer 13 plans hilbertClassField, gal_hilbertClassField_equiv_classGroup and the maximal unramified property. H is CM, hence totally complex, so the narrow and wide Hilbert class fields coincide.

items.name: Λ, the specializations ν_k and the uniformizer π
items.statement: Λ = O_E[[T]]; for k ∈ Z_p the specialization ν_k : Λ → O_E is the O_E-algebra map T ↦ u^{k−1} − 1 for a fixed topological generator u of 1 + 2pZ_p (u = 1 + p for p odd, u = 5 for p = 2), so that weight 1 is the augmentation T ↦ 0. Λ_{(1)} is the localization at (T) = ker ν_1, a DVR in which p is invertible, with uniformizer π = T / log_p u.
items.note: Review note: Status missing is right. The generic pieces (O_E[[T]] as the completed group ring of 1+2pZ_p, weight charts with 1+4Z_2 kept separate at p = 2) are supplied by PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1 and L0a; the paper's ν_k and the normalised uniformiser π = T/log_p u are route-specific (IntegralIwasawaTheoryPartII). Checked: u = 1+p, 5 are the paper's examples ('we may choose'), not requirements.

items.name: π translates orders of vanishing into the weight variable
items.statement: If h ∈ Λ_{(1)} is written h = π^n h_0 with h_0 ∈ Λ_{(1)}^*, and f(k) = ν_k(h) on a small neighbourhood of 1 in Z_p, then f has a zero of order n at k = 1 and f^{(n)}(1)/n! = ν_1(h_0).
items.note: This is why π-adic orders in §5 compute derivatives of p-adic L-functions at weight 1. Review note: Statement checked: ν_k(π) = (u^{k−1} − 1)/log_p u = (k−1) + O((k−1)^2), and ν_k(h_0) is analytic and nonzero near k = 1 for h_0 ∈ Λ_(1)^×, so f(k) = (k−1)^n(ν_1(h_0) + O(k−1)). Elementary; no stage plans it; missing is right.

items.name: The Λ-adic cyclotomic character
items.statement: ε : G_F → Λ^* is the character with ν_k(ε(σ)) = ⟨ε_cyc(σ)⟩^{k−1} for all k ∈ Z_p, given explicitly by ε(σ) = (1 + T)^{log_p⟨ε_cyc(σ)⟩ / log_p u}, where ε_cyc : G_F → Z_p^* is the cyclotomic character.
items.note: Review note: Formula (27) checked: ν_k((1+T)^a) = u^{a(k−1)} = ⟨ε_cyc(σ)⟩^{k−1} for a = log_p⟨ε_cyc(σ)⟩/log_p u, and a ∈ Z_p because ⟨x⟩ = x/ω(x) lies in 1+2pZ_p = u^{Z_p} (also for p = 2). Missing is right; the nearest planned supplier is the universal character of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0a, composed with ⟨ε_cyc⟩.

items.name: Λ-adic Hilbert modular forms and Hida families
items.statement: M(n, χ) is the Λ-module of Λ-adic Hilbert modular forms for F of tame level n = cond(χ) and character χ: for F ∈ M(n, χ) and every integer k ≥ 2, ν_k(F) ∈ M_k(np, χω^{1−k}). S(n, χ) ⊂ M(n, χ) is the cuspidal submodule. M(n, χ) carries Hecke operators T_l for primes l ∤ np and U_l for primes l | np. With Hida's ordinary projector e = lim_{n→∞} (∏_{p | p} U_p)^{n!}, the spaces of Hida families and cuspidal Hida families are M^o(n, χ) = eM(n, χ) and S^o(n, χ) = eS(n, χ). T̃ and T are the Λ-algebras of Hecke operators acting on M^o(n, χ) and S^o(n, χ) respectively.
items.note: Conventions are taken from Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack §§2–3 and Ventullo. PadicFamilies L5 plans ordinary theory over totally real fields and L0a the profinite ordinary projector; neither library has Hilbert modular forms at the pinned commits. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The item copies the paper's slip 'U_l for l | p' (p. 847). The operators U_l for l | n are used throughout: Theorems 3.3, 3.6, 3.8, (37), (42), and §4, where m contains U_l − 1 for l | np. The list should read U_l for l | np. Review note: Planned is acceptable but partial. PadicFamilies:L0a does plan e = lim U^{n!} (profinite ordinary projector). PadicFamilies:L5 plans Hida theory over totally real fields (ordinary loci, control) on integral Hilbert automorphic/cohomology modules. Neither stage explicitly plans Wiles's q-expansion model of Λ-adic Hilbert forms, which is what the paper uses; PadicFamilies:L0 plans that model only for F = Q.

items.name: The Hilbert Eisenstein series E_k(1, η)
items.statement: Let k ≥ 1 and let η be a narrow ray class character of F of modulus b (not necessarily its conductor), totally odd or totally even with parity agreeing with k, excluding F = Q, k = 2, b = 1. The Eisenstein series E_k(1, η) has normalised Fourier coefficients c(a, E_k(1, η)) = Σ_{r | a, (r, b) = 1} η(r) Nr^{k−1} for integral ideals a ⊂ O_F. If b ≠ 1 or k ≠ 1, its constant coefficients are c_λ(0, E_k(1, η)) = 2^{−[F:Q]} L_b(η, 1−k) for λ ∈ Cl^+(F), where L_b omits the Euler factors at primes dividing b. If b = 1 and k = 1, they are c_λ(0, E_1(1, η)) = 2^{−[F:Q]}(L(η, 0) + η^{−1}(λ) L(η^{−1}, 0)).
items.note: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3 plans the Hilbert Eisenstein series, the integral q-expansion principle and the constant-term argument. The b = 1, k = 1 constant term is the source of the extra term in Case 2 and Case 3. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The b = 1, k = 1 constant term copies the paper's footnote 6, which prints χ for η (misprint, recorded under issues). For E_1(1, η) with η of modulus 1 it should be 2^{−[F:Q]}(L(η, 0) + η^{−1}(λ)L(η^{−1}, 0)). Review note: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3 does plan the Hilbert Eisenstein series, the integral q-expansion principle and the constant-term argument, so planned is right. The item's note calls the b = 1, k = 1 term 'the source of the extra term in Case 2 and Case 3'. That holds only when n = cond(χ) = 1. For n ≠ 1, E_1(1, χ) has modulus n ≠ 1, and E_k(χ, ω^{1−k}) has no b = 1 constant term at ∞.

items.name: The Eisenstein Hida family E(1, χ)
items.statement: There is an Eisenstein family E(1, χ) ∈ M^o(n, χ) with ν_k(E(1, χ)) = E_k(1, χω^{1−k}) for all integers k ≥ 1. Here χω^{1−k} is always taken with modulus divisible by all primes above p, so ν_1(E(1, χ)) = E_1(1, χ_S). The constant coefficients of ν_k(E(1, χ)) are 2^{−[F:Q]} L_p(χω, 1−k). E(1, χ) is a Hecke eigenfamily: T_l E(1, χ) = (1 + χε(l)) E(1, χ) for l ∤ np, and U_l E(1, χ) = E(1, χ) for l | np. In particular U_p − 1 annihilates E(1, χ) for every p | p.
items.locator: §3.1, p. 847; its Hecke eigenvalues are stated in §3.3, p. 851
items.note: This is the bridge between the p-adic L-function and the Hecke action; χ_S denotes χ with modulus divisible by all primes of S. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The statement is correct but omits the Hecke eigenvalues of E(1, χ). §3.3 uses them (p. 851: T_l E(1, χ) = (1 + χε(l))E(1, χ), and 'U_{p_i} − 1 annihilates E(1, χ)'), and so do (37), (46) and the construction of Y. Review note: Planned under AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3 is reasonable: the Deligne–Ribet construction is exactly this Λ-adic Eisenstein series, with constant term the p-adic L-function. Its ordinarity and the Hida-family packaging come from PadicFamilies:L5.

items.name: Lemma 3.1 (Ventullo): the auxiliary family G
items.statement: There is a Hida family G ∈ M^o(1, ω^{-1})_{(0)} with ν_0(G) = 1 and c_λ(0, G) = 1 for all λ ∈ Cl^+(F). Write G_k = ν_k(G) ∈ M_k(p, ω^{-k}).
items.note: Proved in Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack under Leopoldt's conjecture using Eisenstein series, and unconditionally by Ventullo (his Theorem 2); cited, not reproved here. Review note: Checked against p. 848: the item matches, including the citation [22, Th. 2] (Ventullo) and the conditional proof in [5]. No stage plans it; missing is right, and the owner is IntegralIwasawaTheoryPartII.

items.name: The forms F_k
items.statement: In Case 1 (R′ ≠ ∅), F_k = E_k(1, χω^{1−k}) − E_1(1, χ_{R′}) · G_{k−1} · L_p(χω, 1−k)/L(χ_{R′}, 0), where L(χ_{R′}, 0) = L(χ, 0) ∏_{p ∈ R′}(1 − χ(p)); if R′ = ∅, F_k = E_k(1, χω^{1−k}) − E_1(1, χ) · G_{k−1} · L_p(χω, 1−k)/L(χ, 0) + E_k(χ, ω^{1−k}) · (L_p(χω, 1−k)/L(χ, 0)) · (L(χ^{-1}, 0)/L_p(χ^{-1}ω, 1−k)). In both cases F_k ∈ M_k(np, χω^{1−k}) has constant terms equal to 0.
items.note: Review note: Statement matches (28)–(29). Constant terms at ∞ are zero, using c_λ(0, G_{k−1}) = 1 and c_λ(0, fg) = c_λ(0, f)c_λ(0, g). When n = 1, the third term of (29) cancels the χ^{−1}(λ)L(χ^{−1}, 0) part of footnote 6. The paper says 'for each integer k ≥ 1', but F_k is only defined for integers k p-adically close to 1: G_{k−1} = ν_{k−1}(G) needs G regular at weight k−1, and (29) also needs L_p(χ^{−1}ω, 1−k) ≠ 0. The item correctly gives no range, and the interpolation (30) is claimed only for k near 1.

items.name: The Λ-adic families F̃ and the element W
items.statement: With L(χω) ∈ Λ_{(1)} the element with ν_k(L(χω)) = L_p(χω, 1−k): in Case 1 F̃ = E(1, χ) − E_1(1, χ_{R′}) G((1+T)u^{-1} − 1) · L(χω)/L(χ_{R′}, 0); if R′ = ∅, F̃ = E(1, χ) − E_1(1, χ) · G((1+T)u^{-1} − 1) · L(χω)/L(χ, 0) + E(χ, 1) · W, where W = (L(χω)/L(χ^{-1}ω)) · (L(χ^{-1}, 0)/L(χ, 0)) ∈ Frac(Λ) satisfies ν_k(W) = (L_p(χω, 1−k)/L(χ, 0)) · (L(χ^{-1}, 0)/L_p(χ^{-1}ω, 1−k)) whenever L_p(χ^{-1}ω, 1−k) ≠ 0. In both cases ν_k(F̃) = F_k for positive integers k near 1, using ν_k(G((1+T)u^{-1} − 1)) = ν_{k−1}(G(T)).
items.note: Review note: Matches (30)–(31); ν_k(G((1+T)u^{−1} − 1)) = ν_{k−1}(G) checked. It uses the family E(χ, 1), which the paper never defines (it defines only E(1, χ)); see the new coverage item.

items.name: Semi-cusp forms
items.statement: F̃ has vanishing constant coefficients at ∞ — in Ribet's terminology it is a semi-cusp form — but is not yet cuspidal.

items.name: The trichotomy of cases
items.statement: ord_π W = r_an(χ) − r_an(χ^{−1}), and F̃ is regular in weight 1 (i.e. F̃ ∈ M(n, χ)_(1) = M(n, χ) ⊗_Λ Λ_(1)) unless W has a pole there. Swapping χ and χ^{−1} inverts W and preserves R′ = ∅. So if W has a pole, one proves Case 3 for χ^{−1}, which gives Conjecture 2 for both characters, and one may assume ord_π W ≥ 0. Case 1: R′ ≠ ∅. Case 2: R′ = ∅ and ν_1(W) ≠ 0, i.e. r_an(χ) = r_an(χ^{−1}); one must prove R_p(χ) = L_an(χ). Case 3: R′ = ∅ and ν_1(W) = 0, i.e. r_an(χ) > r_an(χ^{−1}); one must prove R_p(χ) = L_an(χ) = 0 and R_p(χ^{−1}) = L_an(χ^{−1}).
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The paper and the item gloss 'regular in weight 1' as F̃ ∈ M^o(n, χ)_(1). F̃ is not ordinary in general: it contains the product E_1(1, χ_{R′})·G((1+T)u^{−1} − 1), which is why Theorem 3.2 applies e. The intended condition is F̃ ∈ M(n, χ)_(1).

items.name: Theorem 3.2: F is a cuspidal Hida family
items.statement: There is a Hecke operator t ∈ T̃_(1) with ν_1(t)(E_1(1, χ_S)) = E_1(1, χ_S) such that F = t·e·F̃ is a cuspidal Hida family, F ∈ S^o(n, χ)_(1). Consequently ν_1(F) = ν_1(F̃): this is E_1(1, χ_S) in Cases 1 and 3, and (1 + ν_1(W)) E_1(1, χ_S) in Case 2.
items.note: Cited to Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack, Corollary 2.10 and Proposition 3.4; not reproved. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The published Theorem 3.2 (and so the item) omits the normalisation of t that the later proofs use. arXiv v1's Theorem 3.2 includes it: 'such that ν_1(t)(E_1(1, χ_S)) = E_1(1, χ_S)'. §1.3 (p. 840) also says the cusp family of [5] specialises to E_1(1, χ_S). The published proofs use ν_1(F) ≠ 0: p. 852 'vanish to distinct orders less than r_an', p. 854 'ν_1(F) = (1 + ν_1(W))E_1(1, χ_S) ≠ 0', and Case 3. As printed, the theorem is satisfied by t = 0. Review note: Cited from [5, Cor. 2.10, Prop. 3.4]; not reproved. Missing is right: no stage plans the cuspidality argument. The owner is IntegralIwasawaTheoryPartII.

items.name: r_an and the analytic invariant L*_an(χ)
items.statement: r_an = r_an(χ) = ord_{s=0} L_p(χω, s) (finite, since L_p(χω, n) = L*(χω^n, n) ≠ 0 for every n ∈ Z_{<0}) and L*_an(χ) = L_p^{(r_an)}(χω, 0) / (r_an! · L(χ, 0) · ∏_{p ∈ R′}(1 − χ(p))). If r_an = r then L*_an(χ) = L_an(χ). If r_an > r then L_an(χ) = 0, since the r-th derivative vanishes; this is used on pp. 843 and 867. Conjecture 1 states r_an = r, but that is not assumed.
items.note: The published text writes L_p^{(r_an)}(χ, 0) in this display where L_p^{(r_an)}(χω, 0) is meant; see the source issues. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The statement reproduces the misprint L_p^{(r_an)}(χ, 0) (E3). By PROTOCOL §18, items use the corrected statement, which has L_p^{(r_an)}(χω, 0).

items.name: A Hida family is determined by its Fourier expansion
items.statement: There is a canonical injective Λ_(1)-linear map c : S^o(n, χ)_(1) → ∏_{a ⊂ O_F} Λ_(1), H ↦ (c(a, H))_a; a cuspidal Hida family is determined by its normalised Fourier coefficients.
items.note: The Λ-adic q-expansion principle for Hilbert modular forms, used to define the Hecke orbit module H; stated without reference. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The paper and the item call c a 'Λ-algebra embedding', but S^o(n, χ)_(1) is a module, not an algebra. The mathematical content is an injective Λ_(1)-linear map (the Λ-adic q-expansion principle for cusp forms). Review note: The route assigns it to PadicFamilies:L5, whose description does not mention q-expansions for Hilbert forms; PadicFamilies:L0 plans the q-expansion principle only for F = Q. Missing is the honest status.

items.name: The Hecke orbit module H and the homomorphism ϕ
items.statement: H is the image of the Hecke orbit of F under the reduction of c modulo π^{r_an+1}, a finitely generated module over Λ_{(1)}/π^{r_an+1} = E[π]/π^{r_an+1}, and ϕ : T → End_{E[π]/π^{r_an+1}} H is the resulting canonical Λ-algebra homomorphism.
items.note: The key idea, drawn from Ventullo: F need not be an eigenform modulo π^{r+1}, but its Hecke orbit is finite-dimensional and computable.

items.name: Theorem 2 = Theorem 3.3 (the homomorphism in Case 1)
items.statement: Suppose R′ ≠ ∅ and r = r_p(χ) ≥ 1, and write R = {p_1, …, p_r}. There is a Λ-algebra homomorphism ϕ : T → W_1 = E[π, ε_1, …, ε_r]/(π^{r_an+1}, ε_i^2, ε_i π, ε_1ε_2⋯ε_r + (−1)^{r_an} L*_an(χ) π^{r_an}) with T_l ↦ 1 + χε(l) for l ∤ np, U_l ↦ 1 for l | n or l ∈ R′, and U_{p_i} ↦ 1 + ε_i. W_1 is a local ring with maximal ideal (π, ε_1, …, ε_r) = (T, ε_1, …, ε_r). Here L*_an(χ) = L_p^{(r_an)}(χω, 0)/(r_an! L(χ, 0) ∏_{p ∈ R′}(1 − χ(p))) (see E3).
items.note: This is where the p-adic L-function enters: the relation ε_1 ⋯ ε_r = −(−1)^{r_an}L*_an(χ)π^{r_an} encodes its leading term. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: Tacit hypothesis r ≥ 1 (R ≠ ∅). For r = 0, Theorem 1 is immediate from (3), but here r_an = 0 and L*_an(χ) = 1, so W_1 = E/(2) = 0 is not a local ring. The proof also uses r_an ≥ 1 (so that F̃ ≡ E(1, χ) mod π in the proof of (39)), which follows from (4) once r ≥ 1. The paper never states r ≥ 1. Review note: Proof checked in full (33)–(39), dimension count included. The injectivity step needs ν_1(F) ≠ 0; see theorem-3-2. W_1 is Gorenstein with socle E·π^{r_an} (checked by Gröbner basis for r_an = 3, r = 2), which gives a one-line alternative proof of injectivity.

items.name: The Eisenstein congruence for the second term of F̃
items.statement: π^{r_an} exactly divides L(χω) in Λ_{(1)}, so, since ν_0(G) = 1, F′ = E_1(1, χ_{R′}) G((1+T)u^{-1} − 1) L(χω)/L(χ_{R′}, 0) ≡ (−1)^{r_an} E_1(1, χ_{R′}) L*_an(χ) π^{r_an} (mod π^{r_an+1}), a congruence of Fourier coefficients; hence for τ ∈ T̃, τF′ ≡ (−1)^{r_an} ν_1(τ)(E_1(1, χ_{R′})) L*_an(χ) π^{r_an} (mod π^{r_an+1}), so modulo π^{r_an+1} the Hecke action on F′ only depends on the action on E_1(1, χ_{R′}).
items.note: Review note: Sign checked: f(k) = L_p(χω, 1−k) has f^{(n)}(1) = (−1)^n L_p^{(n)}(χω, 0), so L(χω)/L(χ_{R′}, 0) ≡ (−1)^{r_an} L*_an(χ) π^{r_an}. Also G((1+T)u^{−1} − 1) ≡ ν_0(G) = 1 mod π.

items.name: The Hecke action on the weight one Eisenstein series
items.statement: T_l E_1(1, χ_{R′}) = (1 + χ(l)) E_1(1, χ_{R′}) for l ∤ np and U_l E_1(1, χ_{R′}) = E_1(1, χ_{R′}) for l | n or l ∈ R′; and more generally, for R′ ⊂ J ⊂ S_p and p ∈ S_p, (U_p − 1) E_1(1, χ_J) = E_1(1, χ_{J ∪ {p}}) if p ∉ J and 0 if p ∈ J.
items.locator: §3.3, pp. 850–851 (the T_l and U_l formulas for E_1(1, χ_{R′}) are on p. 850; (35) is on p. 851)
items.note: Called 'a direct calculation'. This is the interesting phenomenon that produces the nilpotents ε_i. Review note: Checked by direct computation. For p ∈ R (χ(p) = 1), c(ap, E_1(1, χ_J)) − c(a, E_1(1, χ_J)) = χ(p)^{m+1}Σ_{r | a′}χ(r) = c(a, E_1(1, χ_{J∪{p}})) with a = p^m a′. The constant terms agree because L_{J∪{p}}(χ, 0) = 0. For p ∈ J the coefficients satisfy c(ap) = c(a).

items.name: The relations ε_i^2 = 0 and ε_i π = 0
items.statement: For p_i ∈ R the operator U_{p_i} − 1 annihilates E(1, χ), so π annihilates the image of (U_{p_i} − 1)F in H and the image of (U_{p_i} − 1)^2 F is 0; writing ε_i for the image of U_{p_i} − 1 under ϕ, ε_i^2 = 0 and ε_i π = 0 for all i.

items.name: The product relation
items.statement: ∏_{i=1}^r (U_{p_i} − 1) F ≡ (−1)^{r_an+1} L*_an(χ) π^{r_an} F (mod π^{r_an+1}), hence ε_1 ⋯ ε_r + (−1)^{r_an} L*_an(χ) π^{r_an} = 0 in End_{E[π]/π^{r_an+1}} H.
items.note: Review note: Correct. The middle step t·e(π^{r_an}E(1, χ)) ≡ π^{r_an}F needs F̃ ≡ E(1, χ) mod π, i.e. r_an ≥ 1, which holds by (4) since r ≥ 1 (tacit; see theorem-3-3).

items.name: W_1 has dimension 2^r + r_an − 1 and ϕ(T) ⊗ E ≅ W_1
items.statement: W_1 is generated as an E-vector space by 1, π, …, π^{r_an−1} and the products ∏_{j ∈ J} ε_j over nonempty J ⊂ R, so dim_E W_1 = 2^r + r_an − 1; these elements act E-linearly independently on F, because π^i F vanish to distinct orders less than r_an at k = 1 and the forms ∏_{j ∈ J} ε_j F are congruent, up to nonzero scalars, to E_1(1, χ_{R′ ∪ J}) π^{r_an} modulo π^{r_an+1}. Hence the surjection W_1 → ϕ(T) ⊗_{O_E} E is an isomorphism.
items.note: The linear independence of the E_1(1, χ_J) for distinct J is asserted as 'easily seen'. Review note: Dimension 2^r + r_an − 1 checked (Gröbner basis: r_an = 3, r = 2 gives 6). The paper prints 2^r here; arXiv v1 printed 2^{r_an}. The independence argument uses ν_1(F) ≠ 0 (see theorem-3-2). 'Easily seen' independence of the E_1(1, χ_J) holds: the matrix of coefficients at a = ∏_{p∈K} p is (2^{|K∖J|})_{K,J}, a tensor power of [[1,1],[2,1]], which is invertible.

items.name: Remark 3.4: the subalgebra T′ and the simpler homomorphism φ′
items.statement: Let T′ ⊂ T be the Λ-subalgebra generated by T_l for l ∤ np, U_l for l | n or l ∈ R′, and U_J = T^{r−#J} ∏_{p ∈ J}(U_p − 1) for nonempty J ⊂ R. The images of these operators under ϕ lie in the E-subalgebra of W_1 generated by π, so restricting ϕ to T′ and reducing modulo π^{r+1} gives φ′ : T′ → E[π]/π^{r+1} with T_l ↦ 1 + χε(l), U_l ↦ 1, U_J ↦ 0 for ∅ ≠ J ⊊ R and U_R ↦ (−1)^{r+1} L_an(χ) π^r; this holds even if r_an > r, in which case L_an(χ) = 0. The map φ′ can be constructed directly from the mod π^{r+1} eigenvalues of F, τF ≡ φ′(τ)F (mod π^{r+1}), and suffices for the applications in §5.
items.note: Only the images of the operators of T′ are needed to expand the determinant in (85) and obtain (87); ϕ on the full Hecke algebra is included for completeness. Review note: Checked: U_J ↦ (log_p u)^{r−#J} π^{r−#J} ε_J = 0 for J ⊊ R, and U_R ↦ (−1)^{r_an+1}L*_an(χ)π^{r_an}, which is (−1)^{r+1}L_an(χ)π^r mod π^{r+1} in both cases r_an = r and r_an > r.

items.name: Remark 3.5: the case r = 1 recovers Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack
items.statement: If r = 1 there is a natural Λ_{(1)}-algebra homomorphism W_1 → E[π]/π^2 sending ε_1 ↦ L_an(χ)π, valid even when r_an > r = 1 (then L_an(χ) = 0); composing ϕ with it gives exactly the homomorphism constructed in Case 1 of Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack.
items.note: Review note: Checked: the relations of W_1 map to 0 when r_an = r (L* = L_an) and when r_an > 1 (L_an = 0).

items.name: Theorem 3.6 (the homomorphism in Case 2)
items.statement: Suppose R′ = ∅, r ≥ 1, W ∈ Λ_(1) and ν_1(W) ≠ 0. Let W_2 = E[π, ε_1, …, ε_r, y]/I_{W_2}, where I_{W_2} = (π^{r_an+1}, y^{r_an+1}, y(π − y), π^{r_an}W − y^{r_an}(W + 1), ε_i^2, ε_iπ, ε_iy, ε_1ε_2⋯ε_r + (−1)^{r_an}L*_an(χ)(π^{r_an} − y^{r_an})). Then there is a Λ-algebra homomorphism ϕ : T → W_2 with T_l ↦ 1 + χε(l) + (χ(l) − 1)((1 − ε(l))/π) y for l ∤ np, U_l ↦ 1 + ((ε(l) − 1)/π) y for l | n, and U_{p_i} ↦ 1 + ε_i.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: Implicit hypothesis: W ∈ Λ_(1) (arranged in §3.2 by swapping χ and χ^{−1}; recalled at the start of §3.4). Only then is ν_1(W) defined, and ν_1(W) ≠ 0 means W ∈ Λ_(1)^×, i.e. r_an(χ) = r_an(χ^{−1}). r ≥ 1 is tacit as in Theorem 3.3. Review note: (41)–(48) checked directly from the eigenvalues of E(1, χ) and E(χ, 1) and the congruence (33). W_2 is Gorenstein with 1-dimensional socle spanned by y^{r_an} (Gröbner basis check, w generic and w = −1), so injectivity is equivalent to Y^{r_an}F ≢ 0, i.e. to ν_1(W) ≠ 0.

items.name: The auxiliary operator Y
items.statement: For a fixed prime q ∤ np with χ(q) ≠ 1, Y = (T_q − 1 − χε(q)) / ((χ(q) − 1)(1 − ε(q))/π) ∈ T̃_{(1)}; it satisfies Y F̃ ≡ π E(χ, 1) W (mod π^{r_an+1}) and Y E(χ, 1) = π E(χ, 1).
items.note: Called an explicit computation. Y is what detects the extra Eisenstein term E(χ,1)·W that appears when R′ = ∅. Review note: Checked: T_q acts on E(1, χ) by 1 + χε(q) and on E(χ, 1) by χ(q) + ε(q), so Y E(1, χ) = 0 and Y E(χ, 1) = πE(χ, 1). Y ∈ T̃_(1) because (1 − ε(q))/π ≡ −log_p⟨Nq⟩ ≢ 0 mod π. Y F′ ≡ 0 mod π^{r_an+1} because ν_1(T_q − 1 − χε(q)) kills E_1(1, χ).

items.name: The relations in Case 2
items.statement: Modulo π^{r_an+1}: T_l F ≡ (1 + χε(l) + (χ(l) − 1)((1 − ε(l))/π) Y) F for l ∤ np; U_l F ≡ (1 + ((ε(l) − 1)/π) Y) F for l | n; (πY − Y^2)F ≡ 0; Y^{r_an+1} F ≡ 0; (π^{r_an} W − Y^{r_an}(W + 1)) F ≡ 0; (U_p − 1)^2 F ≡ π(U_p − 1) F ≡ 0; (U_p − 1) Y F ≡ 0; and ∏_{i=1}^r (U_{p_i} − 1) F ≡ (−1)^{r_an+1} L*_an(χ)(π^{r_an} − Y^{r_an}) F. The computation of the fifth uses E(1, χ) ≡ E(χ, 1) ≡ E_1(1, χ_S) (mod π).
items.note: Review note: All eight relations verified. The item silently corrects two paper misprints: (41)–(42) print 'mod π^{r_an} + 1', and (48) prints ∏_{i=1}^r (U_p − 1) without the index (both recorded under issues).

items.name: dim_E W_2 = 2^r + 2 r_an − 2 and the injectivity in Case 2
items.statement: W_2 is generated as an E-vector space by 1, π, …, π^{r_an−1}, y, y^2, …, y^{r_an} and the products ε_J = ∏_{j ∈ J} ε_j for ∅ ≠ J ⊊ R, so dim_E W_2 = 2^r + 2 r_an − 2; the surjection W_2 → ϕ(T) ⊗_{O_E} E is injective, by a dimension count that treats ν_1(W) ≠ −1 and ν_1(W) = −1 separately and uses ν_1(F) = (1 + ν_1(W)) E_1(1, χ_S) and π^{r_an−1} Y F ≡ π^{r_an} E_1(1, χ_S) ν_1(W) ≢ 0.
items.note: This is the only place the hypothesis ν_1(W) ≠ 0 of Case 2 is used; the construction of the surjection (49) does not need it. Review note: The item's 2^r + 2r_an − 2 is correct: r_an + r_an + (2^r − 2), confirmed by Gröbner basis (r = 2, r_an = 3 gives 8, not 12). The paper prints 2^{r_an} + 2r_an − 2 on p. 854, a misprint carried over from arXiv v1 (recorded under issues).

items.name: Remark 3.7: the case r = 1 in Case 2
items.statement: If r = 1 (so R = S_p = {p}) and w = ν_1(W) ≠ 0, −1, there is a Λ_(1)-algebra homomorphism W_2 → E[π]/π^2 with y ↦ πw/(w+1) and ε ↦ L_an(χ)π/(w+1). Composing it with ϕ of Theorem 3.6 gives a Λ-algebra homomorphism T → E[π]/π^2 with T_l ↦ 1 + χ(l) + ((χ(l) + w)/(1 + w)) log_p⟨Nl⟩ π for l ∤ np, U_l ↦ 1 + (w/(1 + w)) log_p⟨Nl⟩ π for l | n, and U_p ↦ 1 + (L_an(χ)/(1 + w)) π. The paper asserts that this is the Case 2 homomorphism of [5] (not checked here).
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: Two problems, copied from the paper. (1) The images are printed with T where π is meant; π = T/log_p u, cf. (13)–(14), so as printed the coefficients are off by a factor log_p u. (2) 'U_l ↦ 1 for l | n' contradicts Theorem 3.6. There ϕ(U_l) = 1 + ((ε(l) − 1)/π)y, with (ε(l) − 1)/π ≡ log_p⟨Nl⟩ mod π and y ↦ πw/(w+1), so the composite sends U_l to 1 + (w/(1+w)) log_p⟨Nl⟩ π. This is ≠ 1 when n ≠ 1: R′ = ∅ forces n to be prime to p, so log_p⟨Nl⟩ ≠ 0.

items.name: Theorem 3.8 (the homomorphism in Case 3)
items.statement: Suppose R′ = ∅ and W has a zero of order s − t ≥ 1, where s = r_an(χ) and t = r_an(χ^{-1}). With W_3 = E[π, ε_1, …, ε_r, y]/I_{W_3}, I_{W_3} = (π^{s+1}, y^{t+1}, y(π − y), π^t W − y^t, ε_i^2, ε_i π, ε_i y, ε_1 ε_2 ⋯ ε_r + (−1)^s L*_an(χ) π^s), there is a Λ-algebra homomorphism ϕ : T → W_3 with the same formulas as in Theorem 3.6.
items.locator: §3.5, Theorem 3.8, p. 856 (W_3 is introduced on p. 855 and I_{W_3} is displayed on p. 856)
items.note: The proof of Theorem 3.6 constructs the surjection (49) without using ν_1(W) ≠ 0; when ν_1(W) = 0 it is not injective, and factors through the quotient W_3 because Y^{t+1} F ≡ 0 and Y^t F̃ ≡ π^t W F̃ (mod π^{s+1}). Review note: Checked: Y^{t+1}F ≡ 0 and Y^tF ≡ π^tWF mod π^{s+1}; every relation of I_{W_2} lies in I_{W_3} (π^sW ≡ 0 and y^s = 0 there), so (49) factors through W_3. Note t ≥ r ≥ 1 by (4) for χ^{−1}; for t = 0 the relation π^tW − y^t would force W_3 = 0. The paper also uses the letter t both for r_an(χ^{−1}) and for the Hecke operator of Theorem 3.2.

items.name: Injectivity of W_3 → ϕ(T) ⊗ E
items.statement: The forms {π^i F}_{i=0}^{s} ∪ {Y^i F}_{i=1}^{t−1} ∪ {∏_{j ∈ J}(U_{p_j} − 1) F}_{J ⊂ R, J ≠ ∅, R} are E-linearly independent modulo π^{s+1}.
items.note: 'The demonstration of this fact is similar to the previous cases and left to the reader'; see the source issues. It is what makes Theorem 3.8, hence Case 3, complete. Review note: True, and the proof is routine (see E1, rejected). The same leading-term method with powers of Y works: the two forms of each order s−t+i (1 ≤ i ≤ t−1) are separated by applying Y^{t−i}. Alternatively, W_3 is Gorenstein with socle E·π^s (Gröbner basis checks for (s,t,r) = (3,2,2), (4,2,2), (3,1,2)), so injectivity reduces to π^sF ≢ 0 mod π^{s+1}, i.e. ν_1(F) ≠ 0. That needs the normalisation of t that the published Theorem 3.2 omits.

items.name: The prime m and the local Hecke algebra
items.statement: W denotes W_1, W_2 or W_3 in Cases 1, 2, 3, with maximal ideal m_W, and m ⊂ T is the kernel of the composition T → W → W/m_W ≅ E; m is a height one prime generated by T ∈ Λ, T_l − (1 + χε(l)) for l ∤ np and U_l − 1 for l | np. T_{(m)} is the localization and L = Frac(T_{(m)}) its total ring of fractions.

items.name: T_{(m)} is reduced and L is a product of fields
items.statement: Since the tame character χ has conductor equal to the tame level n, there are no n-old forms, so T_{(m)} is reduced; hence there is a canonical injection T_{(m)} ↪ L ≅ ∏_{i=1}^t L_{H_i}, where each L_{H_i} is a finite extension of Frac(Λ) corresponding to a cuspidal Hida eigenfamily H_i.
items.note: The paper stresses that this observation was missing from Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack, thanks Hida for pointing it out, and refers to Hida's 1988 Annals paper, proof of Theorem 3.6 and Corollary 3.7, pp. 381–382. Review note: Source route to PadicFamilies:L5 is plausible (L5 owns ordinary theory over totally real fields, Hida control and residual localization). L5 must then state the reducedness for the cuspidal ordinary Λ-adic Hecke algebra of tame level n = cond(χ) localized at a height-one prime, as here, and not only at maximal ideals; the input is Hida, Ann. of Math. 128 (1988), proof of Th. 3.6 and Cor. 3.7.

items.name: The Hecke algebra of an eigenfamily and its congruences
items.statement: For an integral ideal a, c(a, H_i) ∈ L_{H_i} is the image of T_a; these coefficients generate a finite local Λ-subalgebra Λ_{H_i} ⊂ L_{H_i}, the image of T_{(m)} in L_{H_i} is the localization of Λ_{H_i} at a height one prime m_{H_i} above (T) ⊂ Λ, and c(l, H_i) ≡ 1 + χ(l) (mod m_{H_i}) for l ∤ np, c(l, H_i) ≡ 1 (mod m_{H_i}) for l | np — i.e. the specialization of H_i at m_{H_i} is the weight one form E_1(1, χ_S).

items.name: Theorem 4.1 (Hida, Wiles): Galois representations of Hida families
items.statement: Let H be a cuspidal Hida eigenfamily (tame level n = cond(χ), character χ) with Hecke algebra Λ_H and L_H = Frac(Λ_H), specializing at a weight-one prime m_H ⊂ Λ_H to E_1(1, χ_S), i.e. satisfying (51). There is a continuous irreducible representation ρ_H : G_F → GL_2(L_H), where L_H has the Λ-adic topology (induced by the maximal ideal (π_E, T) of Λ), such that: (1) ρ_H is unramified outside np; (2) for every prime l ∤ np, char(ρ_H(Frob_l))(x) = x^2 − c(l, H)x + χε(l); (3) for every p | p, ρ_H|_{G_p} is conjugate over L_H to (χεη_{p,H}^{-1}, *; 0, η_{p,H}). Equivalently, there is a G_p-stable line on which G_p acts by χεη_{p,H}^{-1}, and the quotient character η_{p,H} : G_p → Λ_H^* is unramified with η_{p,H}(rec(ϖ^{-1})) = c(p, H) for a uniformizer ϖ of F_p. Here rec is in Serre's normalization, so rec(ϖ^{-1}) lifts arithmetic Frobenius. (Theorem of Hida and Wiles: Wiles, Invent. Math. 94 (1988), 529–573, Ths. 2 and 4.)
items.note: Cited to Wiles's 1988 Inventiones paper, Theorems 2 and 4. OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.3 plans the Galois representation over the ordinary Hecke algebra together with its ordinary local structure, including the residually reducible case. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: Part (3) is weakened. The paper, (53), says that ρ_H|_{G_p} is conjugate to the upper-triangular matrix (χεη_{p,H}^{-1}, *; 0, η_{p,H}). So G_p acts on a stable line by χεη_{p,H}^{-1}, and the quotient character η_{p,H} is unramified. The item says only 'reducible with semisimplification χεη^{-1} ⊕ η', which loses which character is the sub and which is the quotient. The ordering is used essentially: the local basis in (64) and (79), formula (80) b = (A_p/C_p)(χη_p^{-1}ε − a), and the definition of v_{p,H} in Lemma 4.3 all depend on it. Review note: Planned OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting:R21.3 is plausible. R21.3 constructs the Galois representation or determinant over the ordinary Hecke algebra with its ordinary local structure, and R21.1 applies the projector to Hilbert Hecke complexes.
