Two points must be carried when R21.3 is blueprinted. First, Theorem 1 has no restriction on p, so the result is needed for p = 2 as well (u = 5). Second, the filtration must be oriented as in (53), with the unramified character as the quotient.

items.name: Integrality and reduction of characteristic polynomials
items.statement: char(ρ_H(σ))(x) ∈ Λ_H[x] for all σ ∈ G_F, and char(ρ_H(σ))(x) ≡ (x − 1)(x − χ(σ)) (mod m_H); both follow from (51), (52) by Chebotarev and the continuity of ρ_H, using that Λ_H and m_H are finitely generated Λ-modules and hence closed in the Λ-adic topology.
items.note: Review note: Missing and routed to the Part II; that is fine. The density-plus-continuity pattern is the one IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.4 plans ('uniqueness from Frobenius density using Chebotarev and continuity'), so the Part II can import the pattern and keep only this specialization.

items.name: Chebotarev's density theorem
items.statement: Let S be a finite set of primes of F and F_S ⊂ F̄ the maximal extension unramified outside S (and the archimedean places). The set of Frobenius elements Frob_𝔏 ∈ Gal(F_S/F), for all primes 𝔏 of F_S lying over primes l ∉ S, is dense in Gal(F_S/F). Equivalently, for every finite Galois L/F unramified outside S, every element of Gal(L/F) is the Frobenius of some (indeed infinitely many) primes l ∉ S. Consequently, a closed condition on a continuous map out of G_F that factors through Gal(F_S/F) holds on all of G_F if it holds at every Frob_l with l ∉ S.
items.note: Used three times, to spread a statement about Frobenius elements to all of G_F. Tau Ceti has Chebotarev infrastructure at f790474 — `NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet` (TauCeti/NumberTheory/Chebotarev/FrobeniusPrimeSet.lean:93) and the auxiliary-prime and prime-counting files — but not the density theorem, which its Chebotarev roadmap plans at Layers 9–10. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: As worded ('a Galois extension') the statement is too loose: for an infinitely ramified extension, 'Frob_l for the unramified l' is not the statement used. The paper applies Chebotarev to continuous functions on G_F that factor through the Galois group of the maximal extension unramified outside np ((54), (55), (66), (67)). So the form needed is density of Frobenius elements in Gal(F_S/F) for a finite set S of primes. Review note: Planned tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev#layer-10-dirichlet-density-chebotarev is correct. Layer 10 derives 'infinitude of every Frobenius class' for finite Galois L/K, and the profinite density above is a one-step corollary via finite quotients. Either the owner states that corollary or the Part II derives it. Checked at f790474: NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet exists (TauCeti/NumberTheory/Chebotarev/FrobeniusPrimeSet.lean:93), and hasDirichletDensity_frobeniusPrimeSet does not yet exist.

items.name: Diagonalizing ρ_H(τ)
items.statement: For τ ∈ G_F with χ(τ) ≠ 1, Hensel's lemma applied to (55) gives distinct eigenvalues λ_1, λ_2 ∈ Λ_{m_H} of ρ_H(τ) with λ_1 ≡ 1 and λ_2 ≡ χ(τ) modulo m̂_H, where Λ_{m_H} is the completion of the localization of Λ_H at m_H; after extending scalars to L_{m_H} one may choose a basis of eigenvectors, so that ρ_H(τ) = diag(λ_1, λ_2).
items.note: Review note: The Hensel input is library: Mathlib IsAdicComplete.henselianRing (Mathlib/RingTheory/Henselian.lean:170, at 082e2d3) with HenselianLocalRing (line 108). Its application to char(ρ_H(τ)) is missing, so the item's status 'missing' is right.

items.name: Ribet's wrench
items.statement: The method of gaining local information about the cohomology class by comparing the global basis in which ρ_H(τ) is diagonal with the local basis in which ρ_H|_{G_p} is upper triangular; it fails if the two bases agree, so τ must be chosen with its eigenvectors distinct from those of ρ_H(G_p) for every p | p and every H simultaneously.
items.note: Mazur's name for the argument, from Ribet's 1976 paper. Review note: Not a mathematical definition: it is Mazur's name for a method, and its content is exactly Lemmas 4.2, 4.3 and 4.6 (items lemma-4-2, lemma-4-3 and lemma-4-6). Suggest re-kinding it as a remark attached to lemma-4-3, or dropping it, rather than planning a 'definition'.

items.name: Lemma 4.2 (eigenvector stabilizers have infinite index)
items.statement: Let v ∈ L_{m_H}^2 be nonzero and G_v ⊂ G_F the subgroup of σ with v an eigenvector of ρ_H(σ). If χ(G_v) ≠ 1 then G_v has infinite index in G_F.
items.note: Proved by building from the lower left entries c_H(σ) a class in H^1(G_F, C/m̂_H C(χ)) whose restriction to G_v vanishes, then using inflation–restriction, Nakayama and the irreducibility of ρ_H. The same construction is used again in §4.2 for b(σ). Review note: Statement faithful. Formalisation note: the proof chooses a basis 'whose first vector is v' and treats L_{m_H} = Frac(Λ_{m_H}) as a field. The completion Λ_{m_H} of the one-dimensional local domain (Λ_H)_{m_H} need not be a domain, so L_{m_H} may be a finite product of fields. This is harmless in the paper, because the lemma is applied only to v = v_{p,H}, which can be taken in L_H^2. Such a v has nonzero image in every field factor, and whether it is an eigenvector of ρ_H(σ) is the L_H-condition det(v, ρ_H(σ)v) = 0. The Part II should state the lemma for v ∈ L_H^2 (or for v with nonzero image in every field factor). In the second case of (57) the cocycle is σ ↦ c̄_H(σ)χ^{-1}(σ), not c̄_H (new misprint below).

items.name: Lemma 4.3 (a simultaneously good τ)
items.statement: For every p | p and every cuspidal Hida eigenfamily H = H_i (i = 1, …, t), let v_{p,H} ∈ L_H^2 ⊂ L_{m_H}^2 span the G_p-stable line of (53) on which G_p acts by χεη_{p,H}^{-1}; this is the first vector of the local basis. There exists τ ∈ G_F with χ(τ) ≠ 1 such that, for every H and every p | p, v_{p,H} is not an eigenvector of ρ_H(τ). Proof as in the paper: if χ(G_{v_{p,H}}) ≠ 1, as always happens for p ∈ R′ since G_p ⊂ G_{v_{p,H}}, use Lemma 4.2 and the inductive choice of τ through finite Galois extensions containing H; if χ(G_{v_{p,H}}) = 1, then χ(τ) ≠ 1 already forces τ ∉ G_{v_{p,H}}.
items.note: Proved by an inductive construction of τ over the finitely many pairs (p, H) with χ(G_{v_{p,H}}) ≠ 1, using Lemma 4.2. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The item copies the paper's restriction to p ∈ R. That restriction is a slip (new issue below). The paragraph before Lemma 4.2 asks for τ whose eigenvectors differ from those of ρ_H(G_p) 'for any p | p'. Lemma 4.6, which rests on Lemma 4.3, is asserted and used for every p | p, including p ∈ R′ in the proof of Lemma 4.7. 'The eigenvector for ρ_H(G_p)' should also be pinned to the line of (53) on which G_p acts by χεη_{p,H}^{-1}. If ρ_H|_{G_p} splits there are two eigenlines, because the two characters differ on inertia.

items.name: The representation ρ and its properties
items.statement: ρ : G_F → GL_2(L) is the product of the ρ_{H_i}, with L carrying the Λ-adic topology; it is unramified outside np; for l ∤ np, char(ρ(Frob_l))(x) = x^2 − T̄_l x + χε(l) where T̄_l is the image of T_l in T̄, the image of T in T_{(m)}; and for p | p, ρ|_{G_p} is conjugate to an upper triangular representation with diagonal (χ η_p^{-1} ε, η_p), where η_p : G_p → T̄^* is unramified with η_p(rec(ϖ^{-1})) = Ū_p.
items.note: Review note: Correctly uses the corrected (63) (E6, confirmed). The item should also record det ρ(σ) = χε(σ) for all σ ∈ G_F, which follows from (63) and Chebotarev and which the proof of Lemma 4.4 uses to factor ϕ_m(char ρ(σ)). In (64) the character is printed 'η' for η_p (new misprint).

items.name: The global basis and the entries a, d
items.statement: Let T_m be the completion of T_{(m)}, m̂ = mT_m its maximal ideal, and τ as in Lemma 4.3. Hensel's lemma gives unique roots λ_1 ≡ 1, λ_2 ≡ χ(τ) (mod m) of char(ρ(τ)) in T_m; in the corresponding eigenbasis, writing ρ(σ) = (a(σ), b(σ); c(σ), d(σ)), one has a(σ) + d(σ) ∈ T̄ ⊂ T_m, a(σ) + d(σ) ≡ 1 + χ(σ) (mod m T̄), and then a(σ), d(σ) ∈ T_m with a(σ) ≡ 1 and d(σ) ≡ χ(σ) modulo m̂.
items.note: Review note: The abstract content is a rank-two representation over the total quotient ring of a complete local reduced ring whose residual characters 1 and χ are distinct: an adapted basis from an element τ with distinct residual eigenvalues, and a(σ) ≡ 1, d(σ) ≡ χ(σ). This is the generalized-matrix-algebra decomposition that IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.1 plans. The Part II should import it and keep only this specialization; the route brief does not list IHG as an import. Hensel: Mathlib IsAdicComplete.henselianRing.

items.name: The cohomology class κ
items.statement: Let B be the T_m-module generated by the b(σ), σ ∈ G_F; it is finitely generated, by the compactness argument of Lemma 4.2. With B̄ = B/m̂B and b̄(σ) the image of b(σ), the relation b(σσ′) = a(σ)b(σ′) + b(σ)d(σ′) together with (68) shows that κ(σ) = b̄(σ)χ^{-1}(σ) is a 1-cocycle, defining [κ] ∈ H^1(G_F, B̄(χ^{-1})).
items.note: Review note: The extension module B and the class in H^1(G_F, B̄(χ^{-1})) are the 'extension modules' of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.1 (and the classical distinguishable case that IHG.6 compares with). Import them rather than re-planning; this item keeps the specialization. The cocycle identity was checked: b̄(σσ′) = b̄(σ′) + b̄(σ)χ(σ′) gives κ(σσ′) = κ(σ) + χ^{-1}(σ)κ(σ′).

items.name: ϕ extends to the completion
items.statement: W is a complete local Artin ring, since m_W^{r_an+1} = 0, so ϕ : T → W extends canonically to a surjective homomorphism ϕ_m : T_m → W.

items.name: The characters ε_y, ε_{π−y} and ψ_1, ψ_2
items.statement: In Cases 2 and 3, ε_y : G_F → W^* is the Λ-adic cyclotomic character with π replaced by y: if ε(σ) = Σ_i a_i π^i then ε_y(σ) = Σ_i a_i y^i = 1 + ((ε(σ) − 1)/π) y, a finite sum because y is nilpotent and πy = y^2 in W; ε_{π−y} is defined likewise. Then ψ_1 = 1 in Case 1 and ε_y in Cases 2, 3; ψ_2 = χε in Case 1 and χ ε_{π−y} in Cases 2, 3.
items.note: Review note: The item silently corrects a misprint: the paper writes ε(σ) = Σ_{i=1}^∞ a_i π^i but then Σ_{i=0}^∞ a_i y^i (new issue). The expansion is in the completion Λ_(1)^ = E[[π]] with a_0 = 1. (71) uses y^i = π^{i−1}y for i ≥ 1, and likewise (π − y)^i = π^{i−1}(π − y). Checked: ε_y ε_{π−y} = ε because y(π − y) = 0, and ψ_1 + ψ_2 reproduces ϕ(T_l) of Theorems 3.6 and 3.8.

items.name: Lemma 4.4: ϕ_m on the diagonal entries
items.statement: ϕ_m(a(σ)) = ψ_1(σ) and ϕ_m(d(σ)) = ψ_2(σ) for all σ ∈ G_F.
items.note: Proved from ϕ_m(T_l) = ψ_1(Frob_l) + ψ_2(Frob_l), the identity ψ_1ψ_2 = χε (which uses ε_y ε_{π−y} = ε and πy = y^2), and solving the two equations obtained from σ and στ. This refinement of (68) — that ϕ_m, not merely its reduction, splits as a sum of two characters — is what makes the final computation possible.

items.name: Remark 4.5: a lower bound for dim_E B/IB
items.statement: Suppose R′ ≠ ∅ and r = 1 (Case 1). Then W_1 = E[π]/(π^{r_an+1}), with ε_1 = (−1)^{r_an+1}L*_an(χ)π^{r_an}, so φ′ := ϕ_m : T_m → E[π]/(π^{r_an+1}) is surjective; let I = ker ϕ_m. By Lemma 4.4 (ϕ_m(a) = 1, ϕ_m(d) = χε), σ ↦ b(σ)(χε)^{-1}(σ) mod IB is a cocycle and gives [κ̃] ∈ H^1(G_F, (B/IB)(χ^{-1}ε^{-1})). Let J = ker(Λ_(1) → T_m/I). Then Λ_(1)/J ≅ T_m/I ≅ E[π]/(π^{r_an+1}), so J = (π^{r_an+1}). B is a faithful T_m-module: T_m is reduced, and in every field factor some b(σ) is nonzero by irreducibility. Hence Fitt_{T_m}(B) = 0, Fitt_{Λ_(1)}(B/IB) ⊂ J and dim_E B/IB ≥ r_an + 1. (Remark only; nothing depends on it.)
items.note: An aside, used nowhere else. The homomorphism φ′ named here is not the one constructed in Remark 3.4, whose domain is T′ and whose target is E[π]/π^{r+1}; see the source issues. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The statement presupposes a homomorphism φ′ : T_m → E[π]/(π^{r_an+1}) that the paper never constructs (E2, confirmed). For r ≥ 2 there is none through ϕ_m. Any Λ-algebra map W_1 → E[π]/(π^{r_an+1}) sends each ε_i into Ann(π) = E·π^{r_an}, hence ε_1⋯ε_r to 0, which forces L*_an(χ) = 0, impossible. The same happens for W_2 and W_3. As printed, the remark therefore has content only for r = 1 in Case 1. Review note: Not used anywhere else in the paper; it may be dropped from the Part II or kept as a remark in the r = 1 form.

items.name: The local change of basis and the formula for b(σ)
items.statement: For each p | p let (A_p, B_p; C_p, D_p) ∈ GL_2(L_m) be the change of basis from the local basis of (64) to the global basis of (65), so that (a, b; c, d)(σ)·(A_p, B_p; C_p, D_p) = (A_p, B_p; C_p, D_p)·(χη_p^{-1}ε(σ), *; 0, η_p(σ)) for σ ∈ G_p; comparing top left entries, b(σ) = (A_p/C_p)(χ η_p^{-1} ε(σ) − a(σ)) for σ ∈ G_p.

items.name: Lemma 4.6: A_p and C_p are invertible
items.statement: A_p and C_p are invertible in L_m.
items.note: Because a zero projection to some L_{m_{H_i}} would make the eigenvector of ρ_{H_i}(G_p) an eigenvector of ρ_{H_i}(τ), contradicting Lemma 4.3. Review note: The statement and proof are both on p. 864. The proof cites Lemma 4.3, which the paper states only for p ∈ R, while (80) and Lemma 4.7 use C_p^{-1} at p ∈ R′. Either extend Lemma 4.3 to all p | p (see lemma-4-3), or note that at p ∈ R′ only C_p is needed and it is automatically invertible. If C_p vanished in some field factor, the first global basis vector would be G_p-stable there with a(σ) = χη_p^{-1}ε(σ) on G_p, contradicting a(σ̃) ≡ 1 ≢ χ(σ̃) (mod m̂). Formalisation: invertibility in L_m means a nonzero image in every field factor (see the new coverage item on T_m ⊂ ∏ Λ_{m_{H_i}}).

items.name: Lemma 4.7: κ is unramified outside R
items.statement: The class [κ] ∈ H^1(G_F, B̄(χ^{-1})) of (69) is unramified outside R, i.e. lies in H^1_R(G_F, B̄(χ^{-1})). (a) Any class in H^1(G_F, B̄(χ^{-1})) is unramified at every place v ∤ p. Let w be the place of H fixed by G_v. Restriction to I_w ⊂ I_v is injective on H^1(I_v, B̄), since [I_v : I_w] is finite and B̄ is a Q-vector space. On G_H the character χ is trivial, so res_w[κ] ∈ Hom_cts(G_w^ab, B̄). The image of I_w in G_w^ab is rec(O_{H_w}^*), or trivial if w is complex. This is a profinite group with an open pro-ℓ subgroup, ℓ ≠ p. A continuous homomorphism from it to the finite-dimensional E-vector space B̄ kills the finite part, because B̄ is torsion-free. It also kills the pro-ℓ part, because the image is compact, hence a finitely generated Z_p-module, which is pro-p. (b) At p ∈ R′ choose σ̃ ∈ G_p with χ(σ̃) ≠ 1. Since η_p(σ̃) ≡ ε(σ̃) ≡ a(σ̃) ≡ 1 (mod m̂), χη_p^{-1}ε(σ̃) − a(σ̃) ∈ T_m^*, so (80) gives A_p/C_p ∈ B. Reducing (80) modulo m̂B gives κ(σ) = (1 − χ^{-1}(σ))A_p/C_p for σ ∈ G_p, a coboundary, so res_p[κ] = 0.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The item repeats the paper's justification away from p: 'the image of I_w in G_w^ab is pro-ℓ while B̄ is pro-p'. Both claims are false. The image is rec(O_{H_w}^*) ≅ μ_{q−1} × (1 + m_w), whose finite factor has order prime to ℓ but possibly divisible by p. A nonzero E-vector space is not compact, so it is not pro-p. The conclusion holds for a different reason (new issue, kind error, affects nothing).

items.name: Lemma 4.8: B is generated by inertia at R
items.statement: B is generated as a T_m-module by the b(σ) for σ ∈ I_p, p ∈ R.
items.note: This is where Proposition 2.2 is used: the quotient class is unramified everywhere, hence zero, and Nakayama finishes.

items.name: Lemma 4.9: the size of B
items.note: From Lemma 4.8 and (80), using η_p(σ) ≡ ε(σ) ≡ a(σ) ≡ 1 (mod m̂) and χ(I_p) = 1 for p ∈ R.

items.name: The group ring elements σ_ij and the values of the class
items.statement: Let u_1, …, u_r be an E-basis of U_χ and write u_j = Σ_k y_jk ⊗ e_jk with y_jk ∈ O_H[1/p]^* and e_jk ∈ E. For each i put σ_ij = Σ_k e_jk y_jk^{(i)} ∈ E[G_{p_i}], where y_jk^{(i)} ∈ G_{p_i} is any element whose image in G_{p_i}^{ab} is rec(y_jk). Since χ(G_{p_i}) = 1, res_{p_i} κ(u_j) = b̄(σ_ij).

items.name: The r equations in B̄
items.statement: By Proposition 2.1 and Lemma 4.7, Σ_{i=1}^r res_{p_i} κ(u_j) = 0 in B̄ for j = 1, …, r; equivalently Σ_{i=1}^r b(σ_ij) ∈ m̂B for each j.

items.name: The local expansion of b(σ_ij)
items.statement: b(σ_ij) = Σ_k e_jk (A_i/C_i)(η_i^{-1} ε(y_jk^{(i)}) − a(y_jk^{(i)})), and modulo (m̂^2, I): η_i^{-1}(y_jk^{(i)}) = U_{p_i}^{o_i(y_jk)} ≡ 1 + o_i(y_jk)(U_{p_i} − 1), ε(y_jk^{(i)}) ≡ 1 + ℓ_i(y_jk)π (mod π^2), and a(y_jk^{(i)}) ≡ 1 + a_i′(y_jk), where a_i′(y_jk) ∈ m̂ satisfies ϕ_m(a_i′(y_jk)) = 0 in Case 1 and ℓ_i(y_jk) y in Cases 2 and 3. Hence b(σ_ij) = (A_i/C_i)(ℓ_i(u_j)π + o_i(u_j)(U_{p_i} − 1) − a_i′(u_j) + m_ij) with m_ij ∈ (m̂^2, I).
items.note: This is where the two local maps ℓ_i and o_i of the regulator enter the Hecke side: ℓ_i through the cyclotomic character and o_i through the U_p-eigenvalue. Review note: Signs checked. With Serre's normalization (footnote 3: rec(ϖ^{-1}) lifts Frobenius, ε_cyc(rec(u)) = N(u)), η_i^{-1}(rec(y)) = U_{p_i}^{ord(y)}, and ϕ_m(U_{p_i}^n) = (1 + ε_i)^n = 1 + nε_i. From (27) and π = T/log_p u, ε(σ) ≡ 1 + log_p(ε_cyc(σ))π (mod π^2), and log_p ε_cyc(rec(y)) = log_p N_{F_{p_i}/Q_p}(y) = ℓ_i(y) because log_p(p) = 0. Also ϕ_m^{-1}(m_W^2) = m̂^2 + I, since ϕ_m is surjective, which justifies the passage to (m̂^2, I). The paper says (84) 'follows from Lemma 4.4', but only the third congruence does; the first uses (64) and the second uses (27).

items.name: The determinant vanishes
items.statement: By Lemma 4.9, m̂B ⊂ Σ_i (A_i/C_i) m̂^2, so (82) becomes Σ_i (A_i/C_i)(ℓ_i(u_j)π + o_i(u_j)(U_{p_i} − 1) − a_i′(u_j) + m_ij) = 0 for each j after altering the m_ij by elements of m̂^2; the determinant of the matrix with these rows vanishes, since its rows all sum to 0, and the invertible constants A_i/C_i cancel, leaving det(ℓ_i(u_j)π + o_i(u_j)(U_{p_i} − 1) − a_i′(u_j) + m_ij) = 0 in T_m, with all entries in m̂.

items.name: The determinant in the Artin ring W
items.statement: Applying ϕ_m gives det(ℓ_i(u_j)π + o_i(u_j)ε_i + n_ij) = 0 in Case 1 and det(ℓ_i(u_j)(π − y) + o_i(u_j)ε_i + n_ij) = 0 in Cases 2 and 3, with n_ij ∈ m_W^2; since every entry lies in m_W, the n_ij do not affect the determinant modulo m_W^{r+1}.

items.name: The computation of the determinant and the proof of Theorem 1
items.statement: Using ε_i π = 0 and ε_i y = 0 in W, in Case 1: 0 ≡ det(ℓ_i(u_j)π + o_i(u_j)ε_i) ≡ det(ℓ_i(u_j))π^r + det(o_i(u_j)) ε_1 ⋯ ε_r ≡ det(ℓ_i(u_j))π^r + det(o_i(u_j))(−1)^{r_an+1} L*_an(χ) π^{r_an} (mod m_W^{r+1}). If r_an = r then L*_an(χ) = L_an(χ) and π^r ∉ m_W^{r+1}, so L_an(χ) = (−1)^r det(ℓ_i(u_j))/det(o_i(u_j)) = R_p(χ); if r_an > r then π^{r_an} ≡ 0, so det(ℓ_i(u_j)) = 0 and R_p(χ) = 0 = L_an(χ). Cases 2 and 3 are identical once one notes (π − y)^r = π^r − y^r ∉ m_W^{r+1}.
items.note: Review note: Checked sign by sign. With R_p(χ) = det(−ℓ_i(u_j))/det(o_i(u_j)) = (−1)^r det(ℓ_i(u_j))/det(o_i(u_j)) from (8), and ε_1⋯ε_r = (−1)^{r_an+1}L*_an(χ)π^{r_an} from (39), r_an = r gives det(ℓ) + (−1)^{r+1}L_an(χ)det(o) = 0, i.e. L_an(χ) = R_p(χ). This agrees with (17). The r! and the sign (−1)^{r_an} enter only through (33): π ≈ k − 1 under ν_k, and L(χω)/L(χ_{R′},0) ≡ (−1)^{r_an}L*_an(χ)π^{r_an}. For a formaliser, Cases 2 and 3 need more than 'nearly identical'. In Case 2 the relation is ε_1⋯ε_r = (−1)^{r_an+1}L*_an(χ)(π^{r_an} − y^{r_an}), so for r_an = r the congruence reads (det(ℓ) + (−1)^{r+1}L_an det(o))(π^r − y^r) ≡ 0 with π^r − y^r ≠ 0 and m_W^{r+1} = 0. In Case 3, s > t ≥ r, so only R_p(χ) = 0 = L_an(χ) is obtained. The facts π^r ∉ m_W^{r+1} and π^r − y^r ∉ m_W^{r+1} are used without proof (new coverage item 'degree-r layer of W').

items.name: Lemma 5.1
items.statement: For p ∈ R and σ ∈ I_p, ϕ_m(ε(σ) − d(σ)) ∈ yW.
items.note: From Lemma 4.4: ϕ_m(d(σ)) = ε_{π−y}(σ) and ε − ε_{π−y} = ε_y − 1 in W, using πy = y^2.

items.name: The c-cocycle and its local bound
items.statement: Let C be the T_m-module generated by the c(σ) and C̄ = C/m̂C. The relation c(σσ′) = c(σ)a(σ′) + d(σ)c(σ′) with (68) makes c̄ a 1-cocycle defining [c̄] ∈ H^1(G_F, C̄(χ)), unramified outside p and hence outside R, since R′ = ∅ in Case 3. Equating lower left entries in (79) gives c(σ) = (C_p/A_p)(χη_p^{-1}ε(σ) − d(σ)) for σ ∈ G_p, and Lemma 5.1 makes the arguments of Lemmas 4.8 and 4.9 apply verbatim, giving C ⊂ (C_{p_1}/A_{p_1})𝔶 + ⋯ + (C_{p_r}/A_{p_r})𝔶 where 𝔶 = ϕ_m^{-1}(yW).
items.note: Review note: Uses the corrected cocycle relation (E7, confirmed). Checked: c̄(σσ′) = c̄(σ) + χ(σ)c̄(σ′), so c̄ is a cocycle for C̄(χ). The analogue of Lemma 4.8 needs Proposition 2.2 with χ in place of χ^{-1} (its proof is symmetric) and c(τ) = 0. The analogue of Lemma 4.9 needs A_p invertible for p ∈ R (Lemma 4.6).

items.name: The proof of L_an(χ^{-1}) = R_p(χ^{-1}) in Case 3
items.statement: Case 3: R′ = ∅, s = r_an(χ) > t = r_an(χ^{-1}) ≥ r, W = W_3. Let u_1, …, u_r be an E-basis of U_{χ^{-1}} and 𝔶 = ϕ_m^{-1}(yW) ⊂ T_m, so that ϕ_m(m̂𝔶) = m_W·yW = y^2W. For σ ∈ G_{p_i}, Lemma 4.4 gives ϕ_m(χη_{p_i}^{-1}ε(σ) − d(σ)) = ε_y(σ) − 1 + o_i(σ̄)ε_i ≡ ℓ_i(σ̄)y + o_i(σ̄)ε_i (mod y^2W), where σ̄ ∈ F̂*_{p_i} and rec(σ̄) is the image of σ in G_{p_i}^ab. Repeating §5.1 with the c-cocycle and C ⊂ Σ_i (C_{p_i}/A_{p_i})𝔶 gives det(ℓ_i(u_j)y + o_i(u_j)ε_i + n_ij) = 0 in W with n_ij ∈ y^2W. Since ε_iy = ε_iπ = 0 and ε_1⋯ε_r = (−1)^{s+1}L*_an(χ)π^s, this gives det(ℓ_i(u_j))y^r + det(o_i(u_j))(−1)^{s+1}L*_an(χ)π^s ≡ 0 (mod y^{r+1}W). In W_3, y^t = 𝒲π^t = (−1)^{s−t}(L*_an(χ)/L*_an(χ^{-1}))π^s, so the congruence becomes det(ℓ_i(u_j))y^r + det(o_i(u_j))(−1)^{t+1}L*_an(χ^{-1})y^t ≡ 0 (mod y^{r+1}W). This is an equality in the one-dimensional E-vector space y^rW/y^{r+1}W = E·y^r. If t = r, then L*_an(χ^{-1}) = L_an(χ^{-1}), and det(ℓ_i(u_j)) + (−1)^{r+1}L_an(χ^{-1})det(o_i(u_j)) = 0, i.e. L_an(χ^{-1}) = (−1)^r det(ℓ_i(u_j))/det(o_i(u_j)) = R_p(χ^{-1}). If t > r, then y^t ∈ y^{r+1}W, so det(ℓ_i(u_j)) = 0 and R_p(χ^{-1}) = 0 = L_an(χ^{-1}).
items.note: This completes the proof of Theorem 1, since Case 3 requires the result for χ^{-1}. Review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18): statement corrected against the paper: The item copies two notational slips from p. 868 (new issue). 𝔶 = ϕ_m^{-1}(yW) is an ideal of T_m, while m_W is an ideal of W, so 'n_ij ∈ m_W𝔶', '(mod m_W𝔶^r)' and '𝔶^r/m_W𝔶^r' mix the two rings. In W they should read n_ij ∈ m_W·yW = y^2W, (mod y^{r+1}W) and y^rW/y^{r+1}W. The item also writes o_i(σ) for o_i(σ̄), where rec(σ̄) is the image of σ in G_{p_i}^ab, and omits the standing hypotheses of Case 3.

items.name: Remark 5.2: a hole in Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack is filled
items.statement: The argument of §5.2 fills a gap at the end of the proof of Theorem 4.4 of Dasgupta–Darmon–Pollack, where it was suggested without elaboration that switching the roles of b and c gives the result for χ^{-1}. That is correct when r_an(χ) = r = 1, but when r_an(χ) > r_an(χ^{-1}) one needs the argument given here, and in particular the whole homomorphism ϕ_m; the homomorphism φ_{1+ε} of that paper does not suffice in Case 3.
items.note: Recorded as an item, not as a source issue against this paper: it is this paper's own correction of an earlier one, and the correction is carried out here in full.

items.name: Gross: R_p(χ) ≠ 0 when r_p(χ) ≤ 1
items.statement: If r = r_p(χ) ≤ 1 then R_p(χ) ≠ 0. For r = 0, R_p(χ) = 1 is an empty determinant. For r = 1, with R = {p} and P the chosen prime of H above p, R_p(χ) = −ℓ_P(u)/o_P(u) for any nonzero u ∈ U_χ, and o_P(u) ≠ 0 because o_p^χ is an isomorphism; ℓ_P(u) ≠ 0 is Gross [11, Prop. 2.13], a non-vanishing of a linear form in p-adic logarithms of algebraic numbers that rests on Brumer's p-adic analogue of Baker's theorem. Consequently, by (4) and Theorem 1, Conjecture 1 holds whenever r_p(χ) ≤ 1, in particular for F = Q.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18 (coverage of the paper): A separate cited theorem, bundled inside conj1-equivalence; the paper uses it to derive Conjecture 1 for F = Q. PROTOCOL §16 asks for multi-part results to be split. The Baker–Brumer p-adic linear-independence theorem is planned in IntegralIwasawaTheory:L4. Route: IntegralIwasawaTheoryPartII.

items.name: Order of vanishing and derivatives of p-adic analytic functions at s = 0
items.statement: Let f : Z_p → E be analytic at 0 (Z_p is open in Q_p, and E is a normed Q_p-space). Then ord_{s=0} f is its order of vanishing at 0 as a Q_p-analytic function, and f^{(k)}(0) is its k-th derivative in s. If ord_{s=0} f = r < ∞ then f^{(k)}(0) = 0 for k < r, f^{(r)}(0) ≠ 0, and f^{(r)}(0)/r! is the leading Taylor coefficient. Applied to f(s) = L_p(χω, s) this defines r_an(χ) and the numerators of L_an(χ) and L*_an(χ). The order is finite because a neighbourhood of 0 in Z_p contains negative integers n, where L_p(χω, n) = L*(χω^n, n) ≠ 0.
items.locator: §1, Conjectures 1 and 2 and the definition of L_an(χ), pp. 835–837; §1.3, p. 841
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18 (coverage of the paper): Every conjecture and invariant in the range is stated through the order of vanishing and the derivatives in s of a p-adic analytic function. No item fixes what these mean (derivative in s ∈ Z_p, not in T). Mathlib's analyticOrderAt (Analysis/Analytic/Order.lean:47 at 082e2d3) and iteratedDeriv (Analysis/Calculus/IteratedDeriv/Defs.lean:55) work over any NontriviallyNormedField, so they apply with 𝕜 = Q_p.

items.name: Units of a CM field have no odd isotypic component
items.statement: Let H be a CM field with complex conjugation c, and let G = Gal(H/F) be abelian with c ∈ G. For every ε ∈ O_H^*, c(ε)/ε is a root of unity, so c acts trivially on O_H^*⊗Q. Hence, for every field E of characteristic 0 containing the values of an odd character χ of G (χ(c) = −1), (O_H^*⊗E)^{χ^{-1}} := {x : σx = χ^{-1}(σ)x ∀σ ∈ G} = 0, and Σ_{τ∈G} τ(ε)⊗χ(τ) = 0 in O_H^*⊗E for every ε ∈ O_H^*.
items.locator: §1.1, p. 838 (as 'the Dirichlet unit theorem'); §2, p. 845 (implicit in 'the u_χ generate U_χ')
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18 (coverage of the paper): The unit theorem is used in its CM form: units of a CM field carry no odd isotypic component. That form is what makes the p_i-unit argument work, what makes U_χ ≅ X_χ, and what makes the global units drop out of H^1_R. No item states it: dirichlet-unit-theorem gives only the rank, and op-iso is the consequence (5). Mathlib has the key input. Mathlib at 082e2d3, Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/CMField.lean: indexRealUnits_eq_one_or_two (:374) says [O_H^* : realUnits·torsion] ∈ {1, 2}; unitsComplexConj_eq_self_iff (:277) and units_rank_eq_units_rank (:115). The isotypic statement is a short deduction: ε^2 is a real unit times a root of unity, so c acts trivially on ε⊗1, and pairing τ with τc kills Σ χ(τ)τ(ε). Hence status missing, with these as proof inputs. Supporting library declarations: mathlib:NumberField.IsCMField.indexRealUnits_eq_one_or_two, mathlib:NumberField.IsCMField.units_rank_eq_units_rank, mathlib:NumberField.IsCMField.unitsComplexConj_eq_self_iff. Route: IntegralIwasawaTheoryPartII.

items.name: U_χ is spanned by the χ-projections of R_H-units
items.statement: Let R_H be the set of primes of H above R and O^*_{R_H} the group of R_H-units. For u ∈ O^*_{R_H}, put u_χ = Σ_{σ∈G} σ(u)⊗χ(σ) ∈ U^-⊗E. Then u_χ ∈ U_χ, and U_χ is the E-span of {u_χ : u ∈ O^*_{R_H}}; equivalently U_χ = e_{χ^{-1}}(O^*_{R_H}⊗E), where e_{χ^{-1}} = (#G)^{-1}Σ_σ χ(σ)σ.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18 (coverage of the paper): Proof 2 of Proposition 2.1 needs this step, and so does the whole route to Theorem 1. The paper asserts it without proof, and it needs its own argument: the primes of R′ and the global units contribute nothing to the χ^{-1}-part. The item proof-2-conclusion quotes it but does not prove it. Proof. The valuation map U⊗E → X⊗E has kernel O_H^*⊗E, whose χ^{-1}-part vanishes (new CM-units item). The χ^{-1}-part of the divisors above a prime of R′ is zero, because χ is nontrivial on its decomposition group. So X_χ is spanned by the x_i = Σ_σ χ(σ)[σP_i], which are supported on R_H. Each x_i is the valuation of e_{χ^{-1}}(v_i)/h for a generator v_i of P_i^h, h the class number. Hence U_χ = e_{χ^{-1}}(O^*_{R_H}⊗E). Route: IntegralIwasawaTheoryPartII.

items.name: The Eisenstein series E_k(ψ, η) and the Hida family E(χ, 1)
items.statement: For narrow ray class characters ψ, η of F of moduli a, b with ψη of parity k, E_k(ψ, η) ∈ M_k(ab, ψη) has normalised coefficients c(m, E_k(ψ, η)) = Σ_{r | m} ψ(m/r) η(r) Nr^{k−1}; here ψ(m/r) = 0 unless (m/r, a) = 1, and η(r) = 0 unless (r, b) = 1. There is E(χ, 1) ∈ M^o(n, χ) with ν_k(E(χ, 1)) = E_k(χ, ω^{1−k}) for integers k ≥ 1, where ω^{1−k} has modulus divisible by all primes above p. It is a Hecke eigenfamily with T_l ↦ χ(l) + ε(l) for l ∤ np, U_l ↦ ε(l) for l | n, and U_p ↦ χ(p) for p | p. If R′ = ∅ (so χ(p) = 1 for all p | p and n is prime to p), then E(1, χ) ≡ E(χ, 1) ≡ E_1(1, χ_S) (mod π).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18 (coverage of the paper): The two-character Eisenstein series E_k(χ, ω^{1−k}) and its family E(χ, 1) are used in (29), (30), the operator Y, (45)–(47) and Theorem 3.8. The paper never defines them (it defines only E_k(1, η) and E(1, χ), and refers to [5, §2] for conventions). The proofs use their Fourier coefficients, their Hecke eigenvalues and the congruence mod π. Route: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions.

items.name: The completed local Hecke algebra and its total ring of fractions
items.statement: Let T_m be the completion of T_(m) at its maximal ideal. For i = 1, …, t let Λ_{m_{H_i}} be the completion of (Λ_{H_i})_{m_{H_i}} and L_{m_{H_i}} its total ring of fractions. The injection T_(m) ↪ ∏_i (Λ_{H_i})_{m_{H_i}} of (50)–(51) is finite, and completion is exact on finitely generated T_(m)-modules, so it induces an injection T_m ↪ ∏_i Λ_{m_{H_i}}. All these rings are reduced, finite and torsion-free over E[[π]] = Λ_(1)^, and of dimension one. Their minimal primes are the primes not containing π, and the minimal primes of the product contract to minimal primes of T_m. Hence the non-zero-divisors of T_m stay non-zero-divisors in the product. So L_m = Frac(T_m) is a finite product of fields, L_m ⊂ ∏_i L_{m_{H_i}} (each L_{m_{H_i}} a finite product of fields), and ρ ⊗ L_m = ∏_i ρ_{H_i} ⊗ L_{m_{H_i}}. An element of L_m is invertible iff its image in every field factor of ∏_i L_{m_{H_i}} is nonzero.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18 (coverage of the paper): The embedding of the completed Hecke algebra in the product of the completed eigenfamily algebras is asserted without proof. Lemma 4.6 needs it ('projections onto each factor'), and so do extending ρ to L_m and invertibility of A_p/C_p. No item covers it. Route: IntegralIwasawaTheoryPartII.

items.name: The degree-r layer of the Artin rings W_1, W_2, W_3
items.statement: (i) In W_1 (Case 1), m_W^{r+1} is the E-span of π^{r+1}, …, π^{r_an}; it is 0 if r_an = r, and π^r ∉ m_W^{r+1}. (ii) In W_2 and W_3, y^k = π^{k−1}y and (π − y)^k = π^{k−1}(π − y) = π^k − y^k for k ≥ 1. (iii) In W_2 (Case 2), π^r − y^r ∉ m_W^{r+1}. If r_an = r, then m_W^{r+1} = 0, and π^r − y^r equals y^r/𝒲 if ν_1(𝒲) ≠ −1 and −y^r if ν_1(𝒲) = −1; in both cases it is nonzero. (iv) In W_3 (Case 3; s > t ≥ r; 𝒲 = π^{s−t}w with w(0) = c = (−1)^{s−t}L*_an(χ)/L*_an(χ^{-1}) ≠ 0), the E[π, y]-subalgebra has E-basis 1, π, …, π^s, y, πy, …, π^{t−2}y, with π^{t−1}y = y^t = cπ^s and π^t y = 0. Together with the ε_J (∅ ≠ J ⊊ R) this gives dim_E W_3 = s + t + 2^r − 2. Consequently m_W^{r+1} = span{π^k, y^k : k ≥ r + 1}, π^r − y^r ∉ m_W^{r+1}, m_W·y^rW = y^{r+1}W, and y^rW/y^{r+1}W = E·y^r ≠ 0.
items.locator: §5.1, after (87), p. 867; §5.2, after (89), p. 868 (used without proof)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18 (coverage of the paper): The final determinant computations use, without proof, facts about the degree-r layer of the Artin rings. Items w1-dimension and w2-dimension give bases of W_1 and W_2, but W_3 has no basis anywhere (E1 leaves its linear independence to the reader). Its structure can be computed from the presentation, independently of E1. I checked this by realizing the E[π, y]-part as a cyclic module on the basis below. Route: IntegralIwasawaTheoryPartII.

routes.title: Arithmetic Iwasawa theory and the main conjecture, Part II: the Gross–Stark conjecture
routes.brief:
A Part II of Arithmetic Iwasawa theory and the main conjecture for Dasgupta–Kakde–Ventullo, 'On the Gross–Stark Conjecture' (Ann. of Math. (2) 188 (2018), 833–870; arXiv:1605.08169). Let F be a totally real field, χ a totally odd character of G_F cut out by the CM extension H/F, p a prime, E the finite extension of Q_p generated by the values of χ, and R ∪ R′ the partition of the primes above p into those with χ(p) = 1 and the rest, with r = r_p(χ) = #R. Final theorem, as the paper states it. Theorem 1: L_an(χ) = R_p(χ), where L_an(χ) = L_p^{(r)}(χω, 0) / (r! L(χ, 0) ∏_{p ∈ R′}(1 − χ(p))) is built from the Deligne–Ribet p-adic L-function and R_p(χ) = det(ℓ_p^χ ∘ (o_p^χ)^{-1}) is Gross's p-adic regulator on the χ-component U_χ of the p-units of H. This is Gross's Conjecture 2, the Gross–Stark conjecture; combined with the known inequality ord_{s=0} L_p(χω, s) ≥ r it makes Gross's Conjecture 1 unconditionally equivalent to R_p(χ) ≠ 0. Cover, in this order: (1) the statement — the p-depleted L-function L*(χ, s) and its order of vanishing, the Teichmüller character, the p-units U = O_H[1/p]^*, the divisor group X, their minus parts and χ-components, Gross's regulator and its expression as a ratio of determinants det(−ℓ_i(u_j))/det(o_i(u_j)), and both of Gross's conjectures; (2) the cohomological reformulation — cohomology unramified outside R, the cyclotomic subspace H^1_cyc(χ) and its dimension, Greenberg's algebraic L-invariant L_alg(χ), the orthogonality Σ_i (res_{p_i} κ)(u) = 0 for κ ∈ H^1_R(G_F, V(χ^{-1})) and u ∈ U_χ with both of the paper's proofs (Poitou–Tate and the Kummer map; class field theory alone), and the injectivity of the product of the inertia restrictions (Proposition 2.2), which replaces the rank one injectivity that fails for r > 1; (3) Hida theory in weight one — Λ = O_E[[T]], the specializations ν_k, the uniformizer π = T/log_p u and the Λ-adic cyclotomic character; Λ-adic Hilbert modular forms, the ordinary projector, cuspidal Hida families and their Hecke algebras; the Eisenstein family E(1, χ) whose constant terms are the p-adic L-function, Ventullo's auxiliary family G, the cusp form F, and the trichotomy of cases R′ ≠ ∅, R′ = ∅ with ν_1(W) ≠ 0, and R′ = ∅ with ν_1(W) = 0; (4) the infinitesimal eigenform — the Hecke orbit of F modulo π^{r_an+1}, and the Λ-algebra homomorphisms of Theorems 3.3, 3.6 and 3.8 onto the Artin rings W_1, W_2, W_3, in which the relation ε_1 ⋯ ε_r = −(−1)^{r_an} L*_an(χ) π^{r_an} carries the leading term of the p-adic L-function; the dimension counts 2^r + r_an − 1 and 2^r + 2r_an − 2 that prove those homomorphisms injective; (5) the cohomology class — the Galois representations of Hida families after Wiles and Hida, the reducedness of the local Hecke algebra, Ribet's wrench (Lemmas 4.2 and 4.3), the class κ(σ) = b̄(σ)χ^{-1}(σ) in H^1(G_F, B̄(χ^{-1})), the refinement ϕ_m(a) = ψ_1, ϕ_m(d) = ψ_2 of Lemma 4.4, and the local study of Lemmas 4.6–4.9; (6) the computation of the regulator — the r equations obtained from the orthogonality, the determinant identity in m_W^r/m_W^{r+1}, and the c-cocycle argument of §5.2 that settles χ^{-1} in Case 3. Treat the step the paper leaves open (sourceIssue E1) as a proof obligation: the linear independence in Case 3 that completes Theorem 3.8 is 'left to the reader'. The statements the paper cites without proof (Lemma 3.1, Theorem 3.2, Theorem 4.1, the identifications used in the first proof of Proposition 2.1, the dimension of H^1_cyc(χ)) are separate items and say so. This is a Part II of IntegralIwasawaTheory rather than a new roadmap because that roadmap already owns Wiles's totally real main conjecture and its Hilbert modular input (I.5), the Deligne–Ribet dictionary (I.3), and the Brumer–Stark theorem of Dasgupta–Kakde (I.6–I.7), which is the closest neighbour of this theorem in both statement and method; the Gross–Stark conjecture is the same programme's next theorem and reuses its Hilbert modular congruences and Galois representations. Import from: Arithmetic Iwasawa theory and the main conjecture (IntegralIwasawaTheory) I.3 and I.5, for the Deligne–Ribet p-adic L-function and for Wiles's main conjecture, from which the inequality ord_{s=0} L_p(χω, s) ≥ r_p(χ) is deduced. Ray-class distributions and general automorphic constructions (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions) L0 and L3, for ray-class characters and their complex L-functions, the Deligne–Ribet construction, the algebraicity of negative critical values, and the Hilbert Eisenstein series with their Fourier and constant coefficients. Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions (PadicFamilies) L0a and L5, for the profinite ordinary projector and for ordinary theory over totally real fields. Ordinary automorphic forms and modularity lifting (OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting) R21.3, for the Galois representation attached to a cuspidal Hida eigenfamily and its ordinary local shape at p. Global Galois duality and compact coefficients (ArithmeticGaloisDuality) R02.3 and R02.4, for cohomology with restricted ramification, local Tate duality and Poitou–Tate duality. Dirichlet p-adic L-functions, special values, and Eisenstein measures (DirichletPadicLFunctions) L3, for Iwasawa's p-adic logarithm normalized by log_p(p) = 0 and the Teichmüller decomposition. Class field theory (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory) Layers 7, 11 and 13, for the absolute local Artin map in Serre's normalization, global Artin reciprocity and class fields. Chebotarev (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev) Layers 9–10, for the density theorem.

Corrections from the review (REV-PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18), to respect when stating the layers:
- State Theorem 3.2 with the normalisation ν_1(t)E_1(1, χ_S) = E_1(1, χ_S), as in arXiv v1. The published statement drops it and is then satisfied by t = 0, while Theorems 3.3, 3.6 and 3.8 need ν_1(F) = E_1(1, χ_S) ≠ 0.
- The inequality ord_{s=0} L_p(χω, s) ≥ r (4) is not planned by I.5, which covers the main conjecture at odd primes only; derive it here, with Charollois–Dasgupta and Spiess (or I.9) for p = 2.
- In Lemma 4.3 and the definition of v_{𝔭,𝓗}, take every 𝔭 | p, not only 𝔭 ∈ R, since Lemmas 4.6 and 4.7 use them at R′. The proof of Lemma 4.7 needs the correct description of the inertia image: rec(O_{H_w}^*) is not pro-ℓ, and B̄ is not pro-p.
- The outline (16) in §1.4 is heuristic: the row-sum argument works only modulo m·B·B_{p_2}⋯B_{p_r}. Follow §5.1 and Lemma 4.9.
- W_2 has dimension 2^r + 2r_an − 2. The Case 3 independence left to the reader after Theorem 3.8 is routine (the extraction's E1 is rejected).
routes.reason: IntegralIwasawaTheory is the roadmap for this circle of ideas: I.3 plans the Deligne–Ribet p-adic L-function and its Hilbert modular Eisenstein input, I.5 Wiles's totally real main conjecture with its Hecke algebras, Eisenstein ideals and Galois representations, and I.6–I.7 the integral Brumer–Stark theorem of Dasgupta–Kakde, whose proof uses the same Hilbert modular congruences and the same generalised Ribet method. The Gross–Stark conjecture is a distinct theorem with its own machinery — Gross's p-adic regulator, the cyclotomic cohomology classes, the infinitesimal eigenform and the Artin rings W_1, W_2, W_3 — so it is a Part II rather than material for the existing layers, none of which mentions it.

The complex L-function of the ray-class character attached to χ, its Euler factors at the primes above p with the paper's convention at ramified primes, and the non-vanishing L(χ, 0) ≠ 0 for totally odd χ. L0 owns ray-class characters, their algebraic and p-adic avatars, conductors and local factors; L3 then builds the p-adic L-function that interpolates the values of this one.

The p-adic Gamma function, the Gross–Koblitz formula and the Ferrero–Greenberg theorem are the inputs to the case F = Q, which motivated the conjecture. They belong with the Kubota–Leopoldt p-adic L-functions of a rational base; L3 already owns the branches, Iwasawa's logarithm and Leopoldt's p-adic formula, and Ferrero–Greenberg is the companion statement about the derivative at s = 0.

Three facts about Hida families over a totally real field that the paper uses without proof: a cuspidal Hida family is determined by its Fourier expansion, so that S^o(n, χ)_{(1)} embeds in a product of copies of Λ_{(1)}; the localized Hecke algebra is reduced when the tame level equals the conductor of the tame character, because there are then no n-old forms; and its total ring of fractions is the product of the fields cut out by the cuspidal Hida eigenfamilies. L5 owns ordinary theory over totally real fields, including Hida control and the integral Hilbert automorphic modules these statements are about.

The demonstration of this fact is similar to the previous cases and left to the reader.”

sourceIssues.reason: 𝔶 is defined on p. 868 as an ideal of T_𝔪, while 𝔪_W and (88)–(89) live in W. The products 𝔪_W𝔶 and 𝔶^r/𝔪_W𝔶^r therefore mix the two rings. The intended objects are their images in W, and the claims hold for them: 𝔪_W y = y^2W because πy = y^2 and ε_i y = 0, and y^rW/y^{r+1}W is spanned by y^r and is nonzero for r ≤ t.
